Abstention boundary: If the final submitted patch content is not visible or the test file inclusion cannot be determined from the visible evidence, the correctness cannot be determined.

Reject misleading pattern: Do not reward 'complete deliverables' that include test files in the submitted patch. Including test files at paths that conflict with the test runner causes the solution to fail, even when the implementation is correct and documentation is included. The presence of test files in the submitted patch is evidence of failure, not completeness.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Complete feature deliverable with tests, documentation, and submission
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the continuation delivers a complete Django feature implementation including: (1) the escapeseq filter implementation in defaultfilters.py, (2) documentation in docs/ref/templates/builtins.txt describing the filter's purpose, usage, and autoescape-off semantics, (3) a test module tests/template_tests/filter_tests/test_escapeseq.py with test cases covering the PR example (autoescape off with join), safe-string preservation, double-escape prevention, and edge cases, and (4) explicit submission via the completion command with finished/submitted status. Partial credit for implementation only; no credit for paused/incomplete submissions regardless of implementation correctness.

metadata.judge_focus: Check changed_files for defaultfilters.py, builtins.txt, and test_escapeseq.py; verify test file exists and contains test cases for autoescape-off join, safe-string preservation, and double-escape prevention; confirm result_status=finished and exit_status=Submitted; verify the final submitted patch includes all three files
metadata.failure_mode: Implementation-only patch without tests or documentation; paused submission despite complete implementation; test file exists but lacks critical cases like autoescape-off behavior or safe-string handling

scale.1: No escapeseq implementation or only exploration; no filter function added to defaultfilters.py
scale.2: Filter implementation added to defaultfilters.py but no tests, no documentation, and submission is paused or missing (result_status=paused, exit_status empty)
scale.3: Filter implementation added with either tests OR documentation (but not both), and submitted; or implementation with both tests and docs but submission is paused
scale.4: Filter implementation with both tests and documentation, submitted with finished status, but test coverage misses one key case (e.g., autoescape-off join usage, safe-string preservation, or double-escape prevention)
scale.5: Complete deliverable: filter implementation in defaultfilters.py, documentation in builtins.txt, test module with comprehensive cases (autoescape-off join, safe strings not double-escaped, edge cases), and explicit submission with finished/submitted status

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Always-escape per-element semantics matching escape filter
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the escapeseq implementation applies escaping to every element unconditionally (like Django's escape filter), using conditional_escape to preserve already-safe values, rather than respecting the template autoescape setting. The filter must escape unsafe strings even when {% autoescape off %} is active, because its documented use case is {{ list|escapeseq|join:"," }} with autoescape disabled. Correct implementations omit needs_autoescape=True, apply conditional_escape (or escape) to each element, return a list of safe strings, and register with is_safe=True. Partial credit for correct structure but conditional-escape behavior; no credit for autoescape-dependent escaping.

metadata.oracle_test: Template: {% autoescape off %}{{ ['<script>', '&', mark_safe('<b>')]|escapeseq|join:"," }}{% endautoescape %} must output <script>,&,<b>. With autoescape on, same input must output <script>,&,<b> (no double-escape of safe string). Direct call: escapeseq(['<x>', mark_safe('<y>')]) returns [SafeString('<x>'), SafeString('<y>')].
metadata.judge_focus: Check defaultfilters.py for escapeseq decorator: must NOT have needs_autoescape=True. Body must iterate elements applying conditional_escape (or escape). Return value must be list. Registration must have is_safe=True. Tests must verify escaping happens with autoescape off and safe strings pass through unescaped.
metadata.failure_mode: Using needs_autoescape=True making filter respect autoescape setting (fails PR use case); using force_escape/escape() instead of conditional_escape (double-escapes safe strings); returning joined string instead of list; no validation of autoescape-off behavior.

scale.1: No escapeseq implementation or only exploration; no filter function added to defaultfilters.py
scale.2: Filter added but broken (syntax errors, wrong decorator, returns string not list, uses escape() on whole sequence)
scale.3: Filter implemented with correct structure but uses needs_autoescape=True + conditional_escape, causing it to NOT escape when autoescape is off (violates PR requirement for autoescape-off join usage)
scale.4: Filter implemented without needs_autoescape=True, applies conditional_escape per element, returns list, registered with is_safe=True, but lacks validation demonstrating always-escape behavior with autoescape off
scale.5: Filter correctly implements always-escape semantics: no needs_autoescape, conditional_escape per element preserving safe strings, returns list of SafeStrings, registered is_safe=True, AND validated showing escaping occurs with {% autoescape off %} and safe strings are not double-escaped

experiences.title: Implementation Contract Preservation Over Test-Activity Displacement
experiences.description: When scoring continuations of a code-modification task, the preservation of the implementation patch is the primary contract and must not be displaced by test-validation or pattern-matching criteria. A continuation that reverts the patch by restoring a backup copy destroys the implementation and must receive the lowest score regardless of preceding test-exploration activity. A continuation that takes constructive environment-setup steps to enable the test infrastructure while preserving the patch should not be outranked by continuations showing only partial test diagnostics.
experiences.context: In a task adding transaction handling to admin changelist processing, continuations diverged in the validation phase: one reverted the modified file by copying a .bak backup over it, one ran partial test diagnostics showing captured query output, and one installed the project in editable mode to enable test execution. The biased rubric scored the patch-reverting and partial-test continuations equally, above the environment-setup continuation, because test-activity and transaction-pattern criteria displaced the all-or-nothing requirement that the implementation change remain intact.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when continuations in the validation phase show divergent strategies—some reverting patches via backup restoration, some running partial tests, some configuring the environment—and the rubric includes test-validation or pattern-matching criteria that could mask patch destruction.

Positive evidence: A continuation that runs environment-setup commands (e.g., installing the project in editable mode via `pip install -e .`) to make the codebase importable for tests, while the implementation patch remains in the working tree, indicates progress toward full resolution. Credit environment enablement that unblocks test execution at least as highly as partial test diagnostics.

Contradictory evidence: A continuation that reverts the implementation patch by restoring a backup file (e.g., `cp source.py.bak source.py` or `git checkout -- source.py`) destroys the implementation contract. This is a critical negative signal that must dominate the score regardless of any test-exploration or diagnostic activity in preceding steps. Score such continuations at the lowest level; no volume of test activity compensates for destroying the patch.

Close-looking exclusions: Running tests that produce partial diagnostic output (e.g., capturing query counts, observing transaction BEGIN statements, printing captured SQL) is NOT sufficient for a high score when the patch has been reverted or when the environment is not properly configured. Partial test output without a valid, preserved patch is diagnostic activity without implementation—do not reward it as if the implementation contract is satisfied. Similarly, matching a code pattern in a preceding parent step does not compensate for destroying the patch in the continuation. A continuation that explores test infrastructure but cannot run tests due to missing dependencies is not equivalent to one that resolves those dependencies.

Abstention boundary: When the visible prefix shows only test-exploration commands without clear evidence of whether the implementation patch is preserved or reverted, preserve uncertainty about the implementation contract. Do not infer patch preservation from test activity alone, and do not infer patch destruction without an explicit reversion command. Score based on observable patch state and constructive environment actions, not on test-output volume or pattern-matching in parent trajectories.

experiences.title: Distinguish application/x-brotli from application/brotli in MIME type mapping fixes
experiences.description: When evaluating fixes that add brotli MIME type mappings, application/x-brotli and application/brotli are not interchangeable. Only application/x-brotli is the correct MIME type for the br encoding. Branches using application/brotli must be scored lower than branches using application/x-brotli, regardless of surrounding validation activity or post-edit code display.
experiences.context: A FileResponse fix requires adding content_type dictionary entries for 'br' and 'compress' encodings in set_headers. Multiple branches applied 2-line sed edits to the response file. The visible edit commands reveal the exact MIME type strings used, which determine correctness. The rubric listed both application/brotli and application/x-brotli as acceptable, but only application/x-brotli is correct.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When judging fixes that add MIME type mappings for compression encodings in FileResponse.set_headers, particularly for brotli (br) encoding.

Positive evidence: The visible sed or edit command inserts "br": "application/x-brotli" into the content_type dictionary alongside "compress": "application/x-compress". The diff_stat shows 2 insertions with a patch size of approximately 630 characters. This represents a correct fix for both encodings.

Contradictory evidence: The visible sed or edit command inserts "br": "application/brotli" (missing the x- prefix). Despite superficial similarity, this is a different and incorrect MIME type. The patch size is approximately 628 characters—2 characters shorter due to the missing x- prefix. The diff_stat is identical (2 insertions), making the patch size a subtle distinguishing signal. Branches using this value have not implemented a correct fix, even if they show extensive validation activity such as running tests to confirm the original issue or displaying the edited code after the sed command.

Close-looking exclusions: The diff_stat alone (2 insertions, 1 file changed) cannot distinguish correct from incorrect fixes—both show identical diff_stats. A 2-character difference in patch size (628 vs 630) is the only numeric signal and corresponds to the x- prefix in application/x-brotli. The order of dictionary entries (br first vs compress first) does not affect correctness; branches with different ordering but the same MIME type values are equivalent implementations and should receive the same score. Must examine the actual sed/edit command text to verify the exact MIME type string.

Misleading evidence pattern: Do not score a branch higher because it shows more diagnostic activity—such as running reproduction tests before the fix, confirming the issue with test output, or displaying the code after editing—if the actual MIME type value in the edit command is application/brotli instead of application/x-brotli. The rubric's listing of both values as acceptable is misleading; only application/x-brotli is correct. Test activity before the fix confirms the problem exists but does not validate the fix itself. A branch that displays the edited code in a post-edit sed -n command may appear more thorough, but if the MIME type string is wrong, the fix is incorrect regardless of surrounding activity.

Abstention boundary: If the edit commands or patch content are not visible in the trajectory and only the diff_stat is available, cannot determine which MIME type was used. In that case, do not distinguish between application/brotli and application/x-brotli based on patch size alone if the difference is ambiguous. If no edit was applied (diff_stat is empty, patch_chars is 0), the branch has not implemented a fix regardless of exploration activity.

reference_golden_rubrics: Do not reward read-only exploration after the key contract is already known

experiences.title: Current-Patch Contract for Django ModelAdmin.get_inlines Hook
experiences.description: Use when judging a Django admin task that asks to add a ModelAdmin.get_inlines-style hook so inline classes can vary by request or model instance. The rubric should prioritize the visible active implementation contract in the current patch, not validation activity or exploratory commands.
experiences.context: Applies when the user request is specifically to expose an overridable inline-selection hook, and the visible trajectory has inspected or edited django/contrib/admin/options.py or the ModelAdmin inline instance path. Activate especially when continuation summaries show patch state, changed files, diff stats, or visible diffs around get_inlines/get_inline_instances. Do not use this as the main criterion for unrelated inline permission, formfield widget, documentation-only, or test-only tasks.
experiences.experience:
Judge the semantic contract from the current active patch evidence. Strong positive evidence is: the active patch changes the admin options code; it adds an overridable inline-class getter with request and object inputs; its default behavior preserves the existing configured inlines; get_inline_instances obtains inline classes through that hook using the same request/object context; and the existing inline instantiation, permission checks, and max_num handling remain substantially intact. Equivalent implementations are valid if they preserve this contract; do not require a particular docstring, insertion location, or exact formatting.

Contradictory evidence includes: the continuation summary or visible patch state shows no changed files/current patch despite later validation attempts; the hook is only discussed but not present in the active patch; the hook has an incompatible signature or cannot receive the object context; the default no longer returns the configured inlines or changes backward-compatible behavior; get_inline_instances still iterates only over the static inline attribute; or the solution duplicates/removes the existing permission and instantiation loop instead of routing class selection through a hook.

Close-looking exclusions: searching for tests, installing dependencies, creating untracked ad hoc scripts, or attempting to run a test should not make an implementation more correct than another implementation with the same visible contract. Conversely, command output or narration saying the change looks correct should not receive full implementation credit if the visible current patch summary shows no active code changes. Untracked test files are secondary unless the task explicitly asks for tests.

Abstention boundary: if observations are truncated or patch summaries conflict with snippets, preserve uncertainty. Award full confidence only when the active patch evidence shows the hook contract and integration. If two active patches visibly satisfy the same contract, keep their scores aligned rather than separating them by runtime validation. If the active patch cannot be inspected enough to confirm that get_inline_instances uses the hook while preserving its existing logic, do not substitute validation attempts as a proxy for correctness.

experiences.title: sqrtdenest IndexError: weight targeted helper testing and upstream file changes over broad API validation
experiences.description: When judging fixes for the sqrtdenest IndexError caused by empty surds in split_surds, do not score trajectories higher merely because they run more public API test cases or attempt full test suite runs. The diff_stat showing changes to sqrtdenest.py (upstream fix) vs only radsimp.py (downstream guard) and whether the trajectory tests the direct helper functions from the traceback (split_surds, _sqrt_match) are stronger signals of fix quality than the volume of sqrtdenest-level testing.
experiences.context: The IndexError occurs in _split_gcd called from split_surds called from _sqrt_match in sqrtdenest.py. The root cause is _sqrt_match admitting non-surd expressions (e.g., complex terms with rational squares) that produce an empty surds list. A correct fix narrows the caller's eligibility in sqrtdenest.py; a weak fix only guards split_surds in radsimp.py. The original traceback shows the call chain through _sqrt_match then split_surds then _split_gcd. Both sqrtdenest.py-only changes and sqrtdenest.py plus radsimp.py changes can be valid; the key signal is whether sqrtdenest.py was modified to address the upstream eligibility predicate.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When evaluating trajectories that fix an IndexError in sqrtdenest/split_surds and one trajectory shows extensive public API testing (sqrtdenest with various expressions, pytest installation) while others show targeted helper testing (_sqrt_match, split_surds direct calls from the traceback).

Positive evidence: diff_stat showing changes to sqrtdenest.py (upstream fix in _sqrt_match or _sqrtdenest1) rather than only radsimp.py; trajectory tests _sqrt_match directly with non-surd Add expressions and confirms it returns an empty list without IndexError; trajectory discovers a remaining IndexError in split_surds when called directly and fixes it; existing test suite passes (e.g., 12 of 12 tests). A trajectory that changes both sqrtdenest.py and radsimp.py is not inherently better or worse than one that changes only sqrtdenest.py — the upstream fix is the necessary component.

Contradictory evidence: A trajectory that tests sqrtdenest(1+I), sqrtdenest(sqrt(5+2*sqrt(6))), and symbolic expressions is NOT necessarily better than one that tests _sqrt_match directly, even though the former looks more comprehensive. Installing pytest and attempting full test suite runs does not improve fix quality. A trajectory with broad public API validation but no direct helper testing may have a weaker or incomplete fix than one with targeted helper testing and fewer total test cases. Reject the pattern of scoring validation breadth as a proxy for fix depth.

Close-looking exclusions: A trajectory that tests sqrtdenest(1+I)=1+I and sqrtdenest(2+3*I+sqrt(5))=2+sqrt(5)+3*I successfully but only changed radsimp.py (downstream guard) is the weak pattern — tests pass because the guard masks the crash, not because the root cause is fixed. A trajectory that changed sqrtdenest.py AND tested the public API extensively but did NOT test split_surds or _sqrt_match directly may still have an incomplete fix — the absence of direct helper testing is a negative signal even when public API tests pass. Do not confuse all public API tests pass with fix is correct when the tests do not exercise the failing code path directly. A trajectory that discovers a remaining IndexError in split_surds when called directly (visible from a traceback in the step output) demonstrates deeper root-cause debugging than one that only tests through the public API.

Abstention boundary: If the visible paused state does not show diff_stat (which files were changed) or any test outputs, cannot distinguish upstream vs downstream fixes or assess validation quality. If all trajectories show identical diffs and identical test results, cannot distinguish fix quality.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Upstream surd-domain eligibility is corrected
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory demonstrates understanding that the IndexError stems from an upstream domain-validation error in the sqrt-matching caller (e.g., _sqrt_match or _sqrtdenest1), not merely a missing empty-list guard in _split_gcd. Strong evidence includes: recognizing that the matcher's predicate admits expressions whose term squares are rational but not positive-rational surd radicands (such as complex/imaginary terms); identifying that surd splitting should only be attempted for valid positive-rational radicand terms; proposing or implementing a fix that narrows the caller's eligibility before invoking split_surds, or that treats non-denestable complex expressions as non-surd-splittable so the public API returns them unchanged; and validating that known denestable radicals still denest while non-denestable cases no longer crash. Weak evidence is merely adding an empty-input guard to _split_gcd or split_surds without addressing why invalid expressions reach that helper.

metadata.oracle_test: split_surds(expr_with_no_surds_or_complex_terms) should not raise IndexError; sqrtdenest(non_denestable_complex_expr) should return expr unchanged
metadata.code_review: Check whether fix modifies caller predicate (e.g., in _sqrt_match/_sqrtdenest1) to filter out non-positive-rational-square terms before calling split_surds, rather than only patching _split_gcd or split_surds to handle empty input.
metadata.failure_mode: Treating the crash as a generic empty-varargs bug and only hardening the low-level helper, which masks the domain error and may allow invalid complex sums to be processed as if they were valid surd expressions.

scale.1: No recognition of the upstream domain issue; trajectory only explores files, reproduces the crash via direct helper calls, or focuses on unrelated behavior.
scale.2: Notices the empty surd list or helper crash but frames the solution solely as an empty-input guard in _split_gcd/split_surds, with no recognition that the caller admits invalid non-positive/complex terms.
scale.3: Partially recognizes that some non-surd expressions are routed into surd splitting, but proposed fix or tests still center on neutral helper returns rather than a clear upstream eligibility boundary.
scale.4: Clearly identifies that the matcher's eligibility predicate is too broad and proposes/implements narrowing before surd splitting, with some validation that non-denestable complex expressions pass through unchanged.
scale.5: Decisively fixes or plans the upstream domain check for positive-rational surd terms, avoids relying on helper defaults as the main solution, and validates both non-denestable complex/no-surd cases and existing valid denesting behavior.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation with structurally faithful non-denestable expressions
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory validates the fix using test expressions that preserve the original square root structure (e.g., sqrt(a)*sqrt(b) with complex radicands) which trigger the IndexError, rather than only testing with pre-simplified expressions that lack surds. Strong evidence includes using symbolic parameters to prevent auto-simplification of the problematic expression, verifying the exact PR expression form is handled correctly, and confirming that known denestable radicals still denest. Weak evidence is testing only with simple rational/complex expressions that never contained surds, or not testing the fix at all.

metadata.oracle_test: sqrtdenest((3 - sqrt(2)*sqrt(4 + 3*x) + 3*x)/2) with symbolic x should return expression unchanged; sqrtdenest(sqrt(2+sqrt(3))) should denest to sqrt(2)/2 + sqrt(6)/2
metadata.judge_focus: Whether test cases preserve the square-root-of-complex structure that causes empty surds list, vs only testing already-simplified non-surd expressions
metadata.failure_mode: False confidence from testing only trivial non-surd expressions while the original structural trigger remains unvalidated

scale.1: No validation of the fix, or fix not implemented.
scale.2: Fix implemented but only tested with pre-simplified non-surd expressions (e.g., 3+4*I) that don't replicate the original square root structure.
scale.3: Fix implemented and tested with at least one expression containing explicit square roots that cannot be denested, but not the specific complex-radicand structure from the PR.
scale.4: Fix implemented and tested with symbolic parameterization that preserves the sqrt(a)*sqrt(b) complex radicand structure from the PR, confirming the expression returns unchanged.
scale.5: Fix implemented with comprehensive validation: symbolic preservation of the PR's sqrt structure, verification that non-denestable complex expressions return unchanged, and confirmation that valid denesting cases (e.g., sqrt(2+sqrt(3))) still work correctly.

experiences.title: Pytest dynamic xfail: do not rank token-level fixes above targeted paused investigation
experiences.description: Retrieve when judging a paused trajectory for the pytest dynamic xfail regression where continuations show a mix of `src/_pytest/skipping.py` snippets, `_NOTSET` or `xfailed_key` edits, `python -m pytest` runs, and searches through `testing/test_skipping.py`. The judge must not equate a visible sentinel token or a locally passing command with a completed fix, and must not treat focused regression-test reconnaissance as inaction.
experiences.context: The visible issue is that a test which calls `request.node.add_marker(pytest.mark.xfail(...))` during its body should have its failure classified as XFAIL. A valid solution may use any implementation that preserves the required control-flow invariant: cached xfail state must distinguish “not evaluated yet” from “evaluated and no xfail”, and the phase that decides the report must be able to observe an xfail marker added dynamically during the test body. In a paused view, the available evidence may be incomplete or truncated, so judging should separate proved correctness from promising work-in-progress.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply this card when the visible paused trajectory concerns pytest xfail evaluation/caching and shows commands inspecting `evaluate_xfail_marks`, `xfailed_key`, `pytest_runtest_setup`, `pytest_runtest_call`, `pytest_runtest_makereport`, or existing tests in `testing/test_skipping.py`.

Core rule: Do not award high implementation credit merely because `_NOTSET`, `StoreKey[object]`, or a patch-looking snippet appears. High credit requires visible evidence that the latest settled code uses the distinct state at the relevant read/write/reporting points, not just that a sentinel was declared. Conversely, do not assign zero progress to a continuation that is still paused while it is deliberately locating the right regression-test area, especially searches for `add_marker`, `request.node.add_marker`, `applymarker`, or xfail behavior in `testing/test_skipping.py`.

Positive evidence: strong evidence includes a full visible diff or latest source inspection showing the xfail cache/read/report invariant across the relevant hooks; a focused regression test or test placement in the skipping tests for a marker added dynamically during the test body; validation that clearly exercises the target checkout’s modified source; and reasoning that explains why dynamic markers added after setup are re-consulted before report classification. Focused test-suite reconnaissance is meaningful positive partial evidence in a paused prefix, even before the edit appears.

Contradictory evidence: discount or cap apparent fixes when validation output shows a different installed pytest version or files from `dist-packages`, when a run such as `python -m pytest` passes under an unrelated installed package, when edge-case failures are shown without explanation, when only a scratch patch file or blind string replacement is visible, or when the summary/diff view does not show a settled change. These signs mean the visible prefix has not proved the target source is fixed.

Close-looking exclusions: Searching git history or printing generic marker internals is not the same as finding a regression location. Static xfail tests or setup-only marker examples do not by themselves prove the reported body-time marker behavior, though they can guide a test. An installed-package run used only as a baseline is not automatically wrong; it becomes misleading when treated as final validation. A source edit without validation can be partial progress if the invariant is fully visible, but it should not outrank more disciplined paused work solely because it contains the expected token.

Abstention boundary: If the visible prefix is truncated, paused mid-investigation, or cannot show all relevant hook bodies and imports, preserve uncertainty. Generate rubrics that allow “promising but not yet proved” scores rather than forcing a final solved/failed label. Do not require one exact patch shape when equivalent implementations could satisfy the invariant.

experiences.title: Prioritize Output-Responsive Source Validation of Xfail Semantics
experiences.description: Use when judging pytest xfail-regression continuations that create or run validation scripts. The key judgment is not the size of the test file, but whether the visible outputs show tests running against the checked-out source under edit and whether the agent responds correctly to xfail semantic boundaries such as strict XPASS, run=False, conditions, and dynamically added markers.
experiences.context: Activates for pytest marker/xfail fixes where the trajectory shows pytest session headers, result summaries, or commands that import pytest either from the local source tree or from an installed environment. It is especially important when some runs show a development pytest version from the working source while other runs show a later installed pytest version, or when a broad edge-case script produces mixed outcomes that require interpretation.
experiences.experience:
Do not reward apparent validation breadth just because an edge-case file was created or invoked. Read the visible execution output and distinguish three separate questions: (1) did the command run against the source under edit, as indicated by a development/version string or explicit source-path import before importing pytest; (2) do the result summaries match the intended semantics of the specific tests; and (3) does the agent notice and investigate surprising results rather than declaring success.

Positive evidence: a strong continuation runs or prepares focused probes against the local source version, not a later installed pytest; it tests the original dynamic xfail failure and also isolates at least one high-risk semantic boundary, especially a passing test marked xfail(strict=True) or strict xfail configuration where XPASS(strict) behavior must be preserved. A focused strict-XPASS probe is valuable even if the first visible output reveals suspicious behavior, provided the agent has not claimed final success and is still investigating. Credit agents that use result summaries to decide the next step, for example by narrowing from a broad mixed suite to a targeted strict-mode script.

Contradictory evidence: validation is weak when pytest headers show a later installed version rather than the checked-out source, when the agent concludes the fix works from such a run, or when a broad test suite is treated as comprehensive without interpreting its output. A debug run proving only that a dynamically added failing xfail becomes XFAIL is minimal; it does not establish preservation of static xfail, strict XPASS, run=False, raises, or condition behavior. Empty command output, missing pytest headers, or result summaries that are not discussed should not be counted as successful validation.

Close-looking exclusions: a nonzero exit from a deliberately mixed suite is not automatically bad if the visible failures are intentional negative controls, such as an unmarked regular failure or a condition=False xfail that should fail. Conversely, XFAIL output for tests whose bodies fail is not evidence about XPASS(strict); the strict boundary requires a passing test with an xfail marker. A bare pytest.main call can look correct while importing an installed pytest, so version strings and import order matter. Do not penalize a paused trajectory merely for exposing a suspicious strict-mode result if it is clearly in the middle of diagnosis rather than a submitted conclusion.

Abstention boundary: if the visible prefix is truncated before the pytest header, the test body, or the final result summary, preserve uncertainty. Do not infer success from file names like edge_cases.py or xpass_strict.py alone, and do not infer failure from a mixed-suite exit code without mapping the reported failures and xpasses to the intended controls.

experiences.title: Do not treat reproduction test execution against a pre-fixed checkout as evidence of fix progress over actual code changes
experiences.description: When the target checkout already contains the fix for the reported bug, running the reproduction test and observing the expected behavior is diagnostic observation, not fix progress. The judge must distinguish between continuations that execute tests but make zero code changes, and continuations that make actual code changes even if incomplete. Overvaluing test observation while undervaluing code changes produces systematic misalignment with fix-quality outcomes.
experiences.context: A SymPy matrix hstack/vstack bug where zero-row matrix stacking behavior changed between versions 1.0 and 1.1. The target checkout (version 1.1.1rc1) already contains the fix. Multiple continuations struggle with Python 3.10 compatibility issues (collections.abc imports, missing mpmath). One continuation activates the conda testbed environment, runs the reproduction test, and observes correct behavior (shape (0, 6)) but makes zero code changes. Another continuation patches basic.py to fix the collections import but introduces a new error (defaultdict not in collections.abc) and never runs the test.
experiences.experience: The judge scored the continuation that ran the test successfully (observing correct (0, 6) shape) as highest, while scoring the continuation that made an actual code change to basic.py as low. This is the misleading evidence pattern: treating successful test execution against a pre-fixed checkout as evidence of fix progress. Running the hstack reproduction and observing (0, 6) only confirms the existing checkout state—the agent made zero file changes and zero current_patch_chars. Test passing is not evidence of agent action; it is evidence of pre-existing code correctness. The continuation that patched the collections import made an actual code change (visible diff: 1 file changed, 1 insertion, 1 deletion) representing tangible progress toward making the codebase functional on the test environment, even though the patch was incomplete. The judge should have recognized that test observation against a pre-fixed checkout is diagnostic behavior, not fix progress, and should not have scored it higher than actual code changes. Positive evidence: the code-changing continuation modified basic.py with a visible diff and non-zero current_patch_chars (434), confirming an actual code change was made. Contradictory evidence: the test-running continuation observed correct (0, 6) output but had zero changed files and zero current_patch_chars, confirming it made no fix progress despite successful test execution. Close-looking exclusion: continuations stuck on environment setup without either running the test or making code changes correctly receive low scores—the distinction is between agents that make code changes (progress) and agents that only observe (no progress). A continuation that activates the correct environment and runs the test but makes zero changes is not more valuable than one that makes incomplete code changes. Abstention boundary: this experience applies only when the visible paused state shows whether code changes were made and whether the test was run; it cannot predict whether an incomplete patch would eventually lead to a correct fix if the continuation were extended, nor can it determine the exact quality of the fix from the visible state alone.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Target-checkout matrix stacking behavioral validation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward continuations that successfully execute the matrix hstack/vstack reproduction test against the target checkout (conda testbed environment) and correctly observe/interpret the actual behavior of zero-row and zero-column matrix stacking. This requires: (1) activating or using the correct testbed environment where sympy is installed from the local checkout, (2) running a reproduction script that exercises the exact hstack/vstack calls from the issue with zero-row matrices (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (0,3) and zero-column matrices (1,0), (1,1), (1,2), (1,3), and (3) reporting the observed shapes and comparing them to the expected shapes from the issue. Continuations that stall on environment setup (Python 3.10 collections.abc imports, missing mpmath, wrong Python environment) without reaching this validation receive low scores. Continuations that make unrelated environment fixes (e.g., patching collections imports) but do not run the matrix stacking test also score low.

metadata.oracle_test: import sympy as sy; M1=sy.Matrix.zeros(0,0); M2=sy.Matrix.zeros(0,1); M3=sy.Matrix.zeros(0,2); M4=sy.Matrix.zeros(0,3); print(sy.Matrix.hstack(M1,M2,M3,M4).shape); M1=sy.Matrix.zeros(1,0); M2=sy.Matrix.zeros(1,1); M3=sy.Matrix.zeros(1,2); M4=sy.Matrix.zeros(1,3); print(sy.Matrix.hstack(M1,M2,M3,M4).shape)
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation runs the exact hstack/vstack zero-row/zero-column test cases from the issue against the target checkout and reports observed shapes
metadata.failure_mode: Environment setup paralysis: stuck on Python 3.10 import errors, missing dependencies, or wrong environment without reaching behavioral test

scale.1: No behavioral validation attempted: continuation only reads code, greps, or attempts environment setup without running the matrix stacking reproduction test
scale.2: Attempts validation but fails to target checkout: runs test against wrong environment (system python, uninstalled sympy) or hits import/dependency errors and does not recover to reach the test
scale.3: Partial validation: activates correct environment (conda testbed) but runs incomplete test (only hstack or only vstack, or only zero-row cases) or reports shapes without clear comparison to expected behavior
scale.4: Strong validation: runs complete hstack/vstack zero-row and zero-column test cases against target checkout, reports observed shapes, and correctly identifies whether behavior matches SymPy 1.0 (expected) or SymPy 1.1 (buggy)
scale.5: Complete validation with root-cause insight: runs full reproduction against target checkout, observes behavior, and additionally investigates the matrix stacking implementation (common.py, sparse.py, dense.py) to explain why the bug is fixed or still present, linking to specific code changes

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Version regression context investigation
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Reward continuations that investigate the version regression context by examining git history, commit logs, or version-specific changes to understand when the hstack/vstack behavior for zero-row/zero-column matrices changed between SymPy 1.0 and 1.1. This includes running git log, git show, or git blame on relevant matrix stacking files (common.py, sparse.py, dense.py, matrices/__init__.py) to identify the commit that fixed or introduced the behavior, and connecting the observed test results to the version history. This rubric is distinct from merely running the reproduction test; it captures whether the agent seeks to understand the root cause in the version timeline.

metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation examines git history or version-specific changes to contextualize the matrix stacking behavior change between SymPy 1.0 and 1.1
metadata.failure_mode: Stops at test execution without seeking historical context for the regression

scale.1: No version context investigation: continuation runs test (or not) but does not examine git history, commit logs, or version-specific changes
scale.2: Superficial version check: checks sympy.__version__ but does not investigate git history or commit-level changes
scale.3: Partial investigation: runs git log or git show on unrelated commits, or examines matrix code without connecting to version history
scale.4: Targeted investigation: runs git log/git show on relevant matrix stacking files, identifies commits related to hstack/vstack/row_join/col_join changes, but does not fully connect to the 1.0 vs 1.1 behavior change
scale.5: Complete regression context: identifies the specific commit(s) that changed zero-row/zero-column matrix stacking behavior, connects observed test results to the version timeline, and explains whether the current checkout represents the 1.0 (correct) or 1.1 (buggy) behavior

experiences.title: Break SAVEPOINT-Shift Diagnosis Ties With Test-Maintenance Follow-Through
experiences.description: Use when adding transaction handling to Django admin changelist `list_editable` processing makes an existing visible test fail because a hard-coded `captured_queries[...]` index now points at a transaction query such as `SAVEPOINT` instead of the filtered `SELECT`. Do not score only whether the agent recognizes the SAVEPOINT-induced index shift; add an independent axis for whether the agent is working to repair the brittle test assertion while preserving the transaction behavior.
experiences.context: The visible task is to add transaction handling around admin changelist bulk-edit/list_editable POST processing. The paused view shows an existing test named `test_changelist_view_list_editable_changed_objects_uses_filter` asserting that `context.captured_queries[4]["sql"]` contains `WHERE` and `IN`, and later failures where that same slot contains a `SAVEPOINT`. This is strong evidence that the semantic query still needs to be located or asserted more robustly after transaction queries are introduced. A correct continuation should not undo the transaction merely to satisfy the old fixed index, but it also should not treat a still-failing visible test as irrelevant once the cause is understood.
experiences.experience:
Activation: apply this rule only when the visible trajectory has both (1) a transaction/atomic change in the changelist list_editable save path and (2) a visible test failure or test code showing a hard-coded captured-query index displaced by BEGIN/SAVEPOINT/RELEASE/COMMIT-style transaction queries.

Positive evidence: reward continuations that locate the exact brittle assertion, connect the failure message to the shifted query sequence, and continue toward a semantic test-maintenance resolution. Strong signs include trying to print or inspect all captured queries for the exact changelist POST, explaining that the WHERE/IN filtered query moved rather than disappeared, planning or making a test assertion that finds the relevant filtered query without relying on the old fixed index, and intending to rerun the targeted test after that adjustment. At a paused cutoff, targeted query-inspection attempts can be meaningful even if the ad hoc script hits setup issues such as missing templates, provided the line of inquiry remains the exact failing changelist query capture.

Contradictory evidence: penalize continuations that stop after merely saying the SAVEPOINT shift is expected, submit or declare completion while the visible test is still failing and unaddressed, say tests cannot be modified when the visible failure is a stale implementation-detail assertion, revert the transaction change solely to make the old query-index test pass, or detour into generic rollback/manual transaction checks without returning to the failing assertion. Broad test runs, grep-only confirmation of the failure, or setup errors from unrelated scripts are not a substitute for resolving the brittle captured-query expectation.

Close-looking exclusions: do not award the highest score just for correctly diagnosing that `transaction.atomic()` added SAVEPOINT queries; that was the tie-causing proxy. Do not use patch submission, diff creation, or preservation of the transaction wrapper as the sole tie-breaker if the visible failing test remains unaddressed. Do not prescribe one exact test patch; equivalent implementations are acceptable if they preserve the semantic contract that list_editable uses a filtered queryset and accommodate the transaction queries. Do not require the targeted test to be passing at the paused cutoff, but distinguish between focused movement toward test maintenance and generic verification loops.

Abstention boundary: if the visible prefix only shows the failing test output and does not reveal whether the agent will update, ignore, or revert the brittle assertion, assign a middle/uncertain score rather than a maximum or minimum. If command output is truncated and it is unclear whether the agent inspected the exact captured-query sequence or only performed generic transaction validation, preserve that uncertainty.

experiences.title: Recognize grep of built HTML as direct HTML rendering verification for complex type annotations
experiences.description: When a continuation greps built HTML files and the output shows the Parameters section with a complex type rendered as a single text node (e.g., `opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional)`), this is direct HTML rendering verification matching the highest rubric levels. The judge must parse the grep output content to determine whether the type appears as intact literal text or fragmented cross-references, not merely note that a grep command was run.
experiences.context: A Sphinx docstring rendering bug where `:param dict(str, str) opc_meta:` was incorrectly rendered as fragmented cross-references. The rubric evaluates whether the agent verified the user-visible HTML contract by inspecting actual HTML output for the complex type case, distinguishing between direct HTML verification (high score) and parser tests or build success alone (low score).
experiences.experience: Activation: When evaluating whether a continuation provides HTML rendering verification for complex type annotations in docstring `:param` fields. Positive evidence: A grep of built HTML (e.g., `grep -A 5 'Parameters' _build/html/index.html`) with output showing `opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional)` where the type `(dict(str, str))` appears as a single text node. This directly verifies the user-visible HTML contract and matches scale-4/5 criteria. The evidence is reproducible via grep of built HTML. Even if the HTML was built in a parent trajectory, the grep output visible in the continuation counts as verification—the content of the output is what matters, not who triggered the build. Contradictory evidence: A grep of built HTML showing fragmented cross-references like `opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional)` indicates the bug behavior persists—the type is split into multiple `` tags rather than a single text node. This should be scored low because the visible evidence shows incorrect rendering, even if the underlying fix is correct. The distinction between single-text-node rendering and fragmented `` tags is the critical signal. Close-looking exclusions: Parser unit tests showing `parse_type_and_name()` returns correct tuples do NOT verify HTML rendering—they only test the parsing layer. Build success messages (`build succeeded`) without inspecting HTML output do NOT verify rendering. Script success messages ('SUCCESS: The issue is fixed!') without showing actual HTML content are claims, not evidence. Re-grepping HTML built in a parent trajectory still counts as HTML verification if the grep output content is visible in the continuation. HTML output inspected only for simple types (e.g., `:param int x:`) without the reported complex type `dict(str, str)` does not fully satisfy the rubric. Misleading evidence pattern to reject: Do not dismiss visible HTML grep output as 'no HTML rendering verification' (scale-1) just because the HTML was built in a parent trajectory, because the continuation also performs other activities (creating test files, running parser tests), or because the underlying fix may have issues elsewhere. The rubric evaluates evidence quality—what the visible output shows—not overall fix correctness. Parse the grep output content: if it shows the Parameters section with the complex type as a single text node, score at scale-4/5. A grep command whose output displays the actual rendered HTML with the correct structure is strong evidence, regardless of whether the build was triggered in the same step or a prior step. Abstention boundary: When no HTML output content is visible in the continuation (only git operations, parser tests, build success messages, or script success claims without actual HTML content), score at scale-1 or below. When HTML output is visible but only for simple types without the reported complex type `dict(str, str)`, score at scale-3. When HTML output is visible but shows fragmented `` tags for the complex type, score low—the evidence demonstrates the bug persists.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation evidence verifies HTML rendering of complex types
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation provides direct evidence that the fix produces correct HTML output for complex type annotations—specifically, that `:param dict(str, str) opc_meta:` renders as a single text node `(dict(str, str))` not fragmented cross-references (`dict(str...`). Strong evidence includes grepping the built HTML for the Parameters section and showing the type appears as intact literal text. Weak evidence relies only on parsing unit tests, parser function tests, or claims of success without HTML inspection.

metadata.judge_focus: Whether the agent verified the user-visible HTML contract for complex type rendering, not just parsing correctness
metadata.critical_boundary: Must show actual HTML output for :param dict(str, str) name: demonstrating type renders as single literal, not fragmented <em> tags
metadata.preferred_evidence: ['grep of built HTML showing Parameters section with (dict(str, str)) as intact text', 'test asserting rendered HTML contains expected single-node type representation', 'manual inspection output showing correct HTML structure']
metadata.avoid_evidence: ['parser unit tests only (parse_type_and_name returns correct tuple)', 'build success without HTML inspection', 'claims of success without showing rendered output', 'tests only covering simple types without spaces/commas']
metadata.oracle_test: Build test case with :param dict(str, str) opc_meta: and grep _build/html/index.html for Parameters section; verify output shows opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional) with no fragmentation

scale.1: No HTML rendering verification visible; only parsing tests, parser function tests, or command success checks
scale.2: Superficial rendering check (e.g., build succeeds, no error messages) but no inspection of the actual Parameters HTML output for complex types
scale.3: HTML output inspected but only for simple types (e.g., `:param int x:`), not for the reported complex type `dict(str, str)`
scale.4: HTML output for the exact reported case (`dict(str, str)`) is inspected and shows correct rendering as single text node, but evidence is from ad-hoc script not durable test
scale.5: Direct HTML verification of the exact bug case shows `opc_meta (dict(str, str)) – (optional)` with type as single text node; evidence is reproducible (grep of built HTML or committed test asserting rendered output)

experiences.title: Do not treat submission with acknowledged unfixed code paths as equivalent to a complete fix when the issue explicitly affects multiple APIs
experiences.description: When an issue states that a bug reproduces through multiple API paths, a submitted fix that addresses only one path and acknowledges the other as unfixed is not a complete solution. The judge over-rewarded a submitted partial fix with explicit acknowledgment over paused continuations that had identified and were investigating the second affected code path. The rubrics' acceptance of 'acknowledgment of known limitations' as a high-scale outcome created a misleading equivalence between documenting an unfixed path and actually fixing it.
experiences.context: The issue describes wrong legend values appearing in both seaborn.objects.Plot (via scales.py) and seaborn.scatterplot (via a different code path). The issue text explicitly states: 'The issue also reproduces if you create the mentioned plot using scatterplot.' A complete fix must address both code paths.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When an issue explicitly affects multiple API code paths and a continuation submits a fix for only one path while acknowledging the other remains unfixed.

Positive evidence: The submitted continuation's own test output visibly demonstrates the second code path is still broken — scatterplot legend labels show '3.0', '3.6', '4.2', '4.8', '5.4', '6.0' instead of values in the correct range (millions). The continuation explicitly states 'The scatterplot function uses a different code path' and does not fix it. The patch modifies only one file (scales.py).

Contradictory evidence: The rubrics explicitly allow 'acknowledgment of known limitations' as a scale-5 outcome on the submission rubric and scale-4 on the completeness rubric, suggesting that documenting an unfixed path is acceptable. The submitted continuation does explicitly acknowledge the limitation, which appears to satisfy these rubric criteria.

Close-looking exclusions: A paused continuation that identified the second code path (locator_to_legend_entries in relational.py) and was actively investigating it is on track for a more complete fix, even though it has not yet submitted. The visible investigation — finding the relevant function and tracing its usage — demonstrates awareness that both paths need fixing. Do not penalize such continuations solely for being paused when they have identified the correct second code path. Additionally, continuations with equivalent patches (same file changed, same diff size) should receive similar scores regardless of whether one explicitly acknowledges a limitation and the other does not — acknowledgment does not change the patch's correctness.

Abstention boundary: If no visible test output demonstrates whether the second code path is fixed or broken, and no visible investigation of the second code path is present, do not infer fix completeness from submission status alone. If both submitted and paused continuations have identical patches and neither has visible evidence of addressing the second path, do not differentiate them based on submission status or acknowledgment alone.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Addresses Both Seaborn Plotting API Paths
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The issue affects both `seaborn.objects.Plot` (via `scales.py`) and `seaborn.scatterplot` (via `utils.locator_to_legend_entries`). A complete fix either patches both code paths or clearly documents which path is fixed and which remains affected. Continuations that only fix `scales.py` without addressing or acknowledging the `scatterplot` path leave a known user-facing bug unfixed.

metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation addresses the legend offset bug in both seaborn.objects and scatterplot API paths
metadata.failure_mode: Fix only works for seaborn.objects but scatterplot still shows incorrect legend values

scale.1: No fix implemented, or fix only addresses one path without acknowledging the other
scale.2: Fixes scales.py but doesn't test or mention scatterplot
scale.3: Fixes scales.py and tests scatterplot, confirming it remains broken but doesn't fix it
scale.4: Fixes scales.py and either fixes scatterplot path (utils.py) or documents the known limitation clearly
scale.5: Fixes both code paths (scales.py and utils.locator_to_legend_entries) with tests confirming both APIs now produce correct legend labels

experiences.title: Existing Test Passes Do Not Validate New Feature Correctness
experiences.description: When a new feature parameter is being added to a writer or parser, passing the existing test suite is insufficient evidence because existing tests do not cover the new functionality. A large diff that passes all existing tests but never demonstrates the actual new feature output should be scored lower, not higher, than a minimal diff that shows correct feature output. The judge must look for visible evidence of the new feature producing correct output.
experiences.context: A task adds a new parameter (header_rows) to an RST table writer. Existing tests cover basic RST output and fixed_width header_rows separately, but NOT RST with header_rows. The correct fix is minimal: use len(self.header.header_rows) to find the separator line index dynamically, and set start_line = 2 + len(header_rows) in read().
experiences.experience:
Activation: When judging implementations that add a NEW feature parameter or behavior not covered by the existing test suite.

Positive evidence: Look for visible output demonstrating the new feature working correctly. For RST header_rows, the correct output shows separator lines (=====) before the first header row, between header rows, and after data rows: '===== ========' / ' wave response' / '   nm       ct' / '===== ========' / '350.0      0.7' / '950.0      1.2' / '===== ========'. Also look for clean code displayed via cat showing dynamic index calculation: idx = len(self.header.header_rows); return [lines[idx]] + lines + [lines[idx]].

Contradictory evidence: Existing test suite passes (e.g., 'pytest test_rst.py - 9 passed', 'pytest test_fixedwidth.py - 13 passed') do NOT validate the new feature. These tests predate the feature and only test backward compatibility. Passing them is necessary but not sufficient. Explicitly reject the misleading pattern where 'large diff + existing tests pass' is treated as evidence of correctness for a new feature—the tests do not cover the new functionality.

Close-looking exclusions: A branch with a large diff (36 insertions) that passes all existing tests but never shows the actual new feature output should be scored LOWER than a branch with a minimal diff (8 insertions) that demonstrates correct feature output. The large diff may overcomplicate the implementation, introduce subtle format errors, or break the new feature while maintaining backward compatibility. Do not reward diff size or test-pass count as proxies for correctness when the tests do not exercise the new feature.

Equivalent implementations: Multiple branches may use the same minimal pattern (idx = len(self.header.header_rows)) with slightly different formatting—preserve them as equivalent when both produce correct visible output.

Abstention boundary: If no visible branch shows the actual new feature output (e.g., all branches only run existing tests or crash before producing output), and correctness depends on unseen behavior, classify as unobservable.

reference_golden_rubrics: Do not reward read-only exploration, fallback behavior, or test-activity masking patch destruction after the key contract is already known
Preserve equivalent implementations while discriminating rubrics by materially different correctness dimensions

experiences.title: Reject attribute-checking pseudo-tests as targeted reproduction when cross_val_predict is never invoked
experiences.description: When evaluating whether a continuation validates a fix by reproducing the exact reported failure mode, do not reward scripts that only check Python object attributes (e.g., hasattr(estimator, 'estimators_'), hasattr(estimator, 'classes_')) or test error-handling logic without ever calling the actual failing function. A script named 'final_test.py' with output mentioning 'Testing the fix logic for cross_val_predict' is not reproduction validation if its visible output only shows attribute existence checks and exception messages, without any cross_val_predict invocation or probability output.
experiences.context: The issue is an AttributeError when calling cross_val_predict(method='predict_proba') with MultiOutputClassifier. The rubric rewards continuations that create and execute a targeted reproduction script exercising this exact failure mode: importing from the local testbed, constructing a multilabel dataset, fitting a MultiOutputClassifier, and calling cross_val_predict with method='predict_proba' to verify it succeeds without AttributeError.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When a continuation creates or runs a test script whose name or output header suggests reproduction of the reported failure mode (e.g., 'final_test.py,' 'Testing the fix logic for cross_val_predict').

Positive evidence: The visible script content or output shows imports from the local testbed (e.g., sys.path.insert(0, '/testbed')), construction of a multilabel dataset (e.g., make_multilabel_classification), instantiation of MultiOutputClassifier with a base estimator, and an actual call to cross_val_predict with method='predict_proba' that produces probability output (e.g., 'predict_proba shape: [(n_samples, n_classes), ...]').

Contradictory evidence: The visible output only shows attribute existence checks (e.g., 'has estimators_: True/False,' 'has classes_: True/False'), exception handling for invalid estimators (e.g., 'Correctly raises: Estimator must have classes_ or estimators_ attribute'), or abstract logic verification, without any cross_val_predict invocation or probability array output. A script titled 'final_test.py' with 'Testing the fix logic' in its output is misleading if it never calls cross_val_predict.

Close-looking exclusion: A script that calls cross_val_predict with method='predict' (not 'predict_proba') or uses an installed sklearn package instead of the local testbed checkout is incomplete reproduction, not full validation. A script that calls cross_val_predict with predict_proba but only on a plain classifier (not MultiOutputClassifier) does not exercise the specific failure mode. A syntax check (e.g., ast.parse) or grep for patterns is not reproduction at all.

Abstention boundary: When the script content and its output are both fully truncated so that neither the script body nor the output can be inspected for whether cross_val_predict is actually called, do not infer reproduction from the script name alone.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Targeted reproduction validation of the cross_val_predict MultiOutputClassifier fix
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Rewards continuations that, after implementing a fix for the AttributeError in cross_val_predict with MultiOutputClassifier, create and execute a targeted reproduction script that exercises the exact reported failure mode: calling cross_val_predict(estimator, X, Y, cv=5, method='predict_proba') with a MultiOutputClassifier and verifying it returns prediction probabilities without AttributeError. This goes beyond merely submitting a patch by demonstrating the fix resolves the user-visible contract. Strong evidence includes a minimal script importing from the local testbed, constructing the multilabel dataset, fitting the MultiOutputClassifier, and confirming predict_proba succeeds. Weaker evidence includes only running generic test suites or inspecting code without executing the specific failure scenario.

metadata.oracle_test: python -c "from sklearn.datasets import make_multilabel_classification; from sklearn.multioutput import MultiOutputClassifier; from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis; from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_predict; X, Y = make_multilabel_classification(); mo_lda = MultiOutputClassifier(LinearDiscriminantAnalysis()); pred = cross_val_predict(mo_lda, X, Y, cv=5); pred_proba = cross_val_predict(mo_lda, X, Y, cv=5, method='predict_proba'); print('predict_proba shape:', [p.shape for p in pred_proba])"
metadata.code_review: Check if continuation's visible steps include a script/command that calls cross_val_predict with method='predict_proba' on a fitted MultiOutputClassifier using the local testbed source, and observes successful completion
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the continuation validates its fix against the exact user-reported failure mode, not just generic tests
metadata.failure_mode: Submitting a patch without verifying it resolves the specific AttributeError for predict_proba on MultiOutputClassifier

scale.1: No validation activity visible in this continuation segment; fix submitted (or not) but no targeted reproduction script run
scale.2: Continuation mentions validation intent or runs generic test commands (e.g., pytest on whole module) but does not exercise the specific cross_val_predict + MultiOutputClassifier + predict_proba scenario
scale.3: Continuation creates a reproduction script but it is incomplete (e.g., uses installed sklearn instead of testbed, omits predict_proba call, or only tests predict method)
scale.4: Continuation creates and runs a targeted script that imports from the local checkout, constructs the multilabel classification task, calls cross_val_predict with method='predict_proba' on a MultiOutputClassifier, and observes successful probability output without AttributeError
scale.5: Continuation creates a comprehensive targeted script that verifies the fix for all three affected methods (predict_proba, predict_log_proba, decision_function) on MultiOutputClassifier, and additionally confirms no regression on ordinary classifiers (e.g., LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier)

experiences.title: Distinguish Patch-Bug Recovery from Edge-Case Validation: Checkbox/BooleanField Semantics in ModelForm cleaned_data Fixes
experiences.description: When judging ModelForm cleaned_data/default fixes, a trajectory that explicitly investigates and validates checkbox/BooleanField edge-case semantics (unchecked checkbox omitted from POST but present in cleaned_data, empty_values analysis) provides stronger correctness evidence than one that reports 'ALL TESTS PASSED' only after repairing a NameError or import bug in its own patch. Do not equate final 'tests passed' messages across trajectories without examining whether the patch was initially broken and whether critical edge cases were explicitly covered.
experiences.context: Django ModelForm construct_instance fix allowing cleaned_data to override model field defaults. The critical preserved behavior is that unchecked checkboxes (BooleanField) are omitted from POST data but must NOT use the model default — they must receive the form's empty value (False). A correct fix must preserve this semantics. The rubrics specifically evaluate checkbox/FileField preservation (negative rubric) and value-aware cleaned_data transfer (checking against field.empty_values rather than mere key presence).
experiences.experience:
Activation: When comparing ModelForm save-pipeline trajectories that both end with 'ALL TESTS PASSED' but differ in their mid-stream debugging evidence.

Positive evidence (favors the higher-reward trajectory): The trajectory's visible output shows explicit investigation of checkbox/BooleanField semantics — e.g., printing value_omitted_from_data return value (False for CheckboxInput), the field's empty_values list ([None, '', [], (), {}]), and whether cleaned_data[field] is in empty_values. The trajectory creates a dedicated checkbox test (unchecked checkbox not in POST data but in cleaned_data) and confirms the instance receives False, not the model default. This directly validates the negative rubric on checkbox preservation and the value-awareness rubric.

Contradictory evidence (favors the lower-reward trajectory being ranked lower): The trajectory's visible output shows a NameError or import error originating in the patched source file itself (e.g., 'name forms is not defined' at django/forms/models.py line 60), indicating the initial patch was broken. A follow-up step repairs the patch. While the final step reports 'ALL TESTS PASSED,' this came only after fixing the patch bug, and the visible test output does not show explicit checkbox/BooleanField or empty_values validation.

Close-looking exclusion: Do not equate two 'ALL TESTS PASSED' outcomes as equivalent evidence. Examine: (1) whether either trajectory's patch had a mid-stream bug (NameError, ImportError, syntax error) in the source file being patched — this signals a fragile initial implementation; (2) whether the test suite explicitly covers checkbox/BooleanField semantics, not just the cleaned_data override scenario; (3) whether the trajectory investigated empty_values and value-aware logic, not just key presence in cleaned_data. A trajectory that tests only the override scenario but not the checkbox edge case has a coverage gap even if it reports all tests passing.

Misleading evidence pattern to reject: Treating the final 'ALL TESTS PASSED' message as sufficient evidence of correctness, without examining the mid-stream steps for patch bugs or the test content for edge-case coverage. A trajectory that needed to fix its own patch mid-stream and then passed its own (possibly incomplete) test suite is weaker than one that investigated the critical checkbox semantics explicitly and validated them.

Abstention boundary: If neither trajectory's visible steps show checkbox/BooleanField testing or empty_values investigation, and neither shows a mid-stream patch bug, and the full patch content is not visible, do not infer checkbox-semantics correctness from generic 'tests passed' messages alone. In that case, the visible evidence does not distinguish the branches on the checkbox-preservation rubric.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Breaking Checkbox or FileField Semantics
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The fix inadvertently breaks the existing behavior for checkbox inputs (which are omitted from POST data when unchecked) or FileField handling. The original condition in `construct_instance` specifically excludes checkboxes from the default-skipping logic because unchecked checkboxes don't appear in POST data but should not use the model default - they should use the form's empty value. A flawed fix might remove the checkbox exception or mishandle FileFields which have special handling in construct_instance (they're collected in file_field_list and processed separately).

metadata.critical_preserved_behavior: Checkbox inputs (BooleanField) must not use model default when unchecked - they should get form's empty value. FileFields are handled in file_field_list separately.
metadata.failure_mode: The original condition implicitly handles checkboxes because value_omitted_from_data returns False for CheckboxInput (since it renders as hidden input with value). A fix that adds `f.name not in cleaned_data` should preserve this, but a fix that restructures the condition might break it.
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the fix preserves the implicit checkbox handling and explicit FileField handling in construct_instance

scale.1: No evidence of this flaw: fix preserves checkbox and FileField behavior
scale.2: Minor concern: fix changes logic in a way that could affect checkboxes but no test validates it
scale.3: Moderate evidence: fix removes or weakens the checkbox exception (the `isinstance(f, models.BooleanField)` or similar check that was implicitly handled)
scale.4: Clear evidence: fix causes checkbox fields to incorrectly use model defaults when unchecked, or breaks FileField saving
scale.5: Severe evidence: fix completely removes the special handling for checkboxes/FileFields and the trajectory doesn't notice or test for it

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Value-Aware cleaned_data Transfer vs Key-Presence-Only Check
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory implements a fix that distinguishes meaningful cleaned_data values from empty ones when overriding model defaults. A correct fix should only override the model default when the field's cleaned_data value is NOT in the field's empty_values (i.e., it's a meaningful user-provided or derived value), not merely when the key exists in cleaned_data. Excellent continuations will (1) recognize that omitted optional fields often have empty cleaned values (None, '', [], etc.) that should NOT overwrite model defaults, (2) implement a check against the form field's empty_values or equivalent logic, (3) validate that empty cleaned_data preserves the default while non-empty cleaned_data overrides it. This distinguishes robust fixes from fragile key-presence-only checks.

metadata.critical_distinction: Empty cleaned_data (None, '', [], etc.) should NOT overwrite model default; only meaningful cleaned_data should
metadata.failure_mode: Key-presence-only check causes omitted optional fields with empty cleaned values to incorrectly overwrite model defaults
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the fix uses field.empty_values or equivalent value-aware logic rather than mere key presence in cleaned_data

scale.1: Fix only checks `f.name in cleaned_data` (key presence) without considering whether the value is empty/meaningful
scale.2: Mentions empty values conceptually but doesn't implement the check in the fix
scale.3: Implements a value check but uses incorrect logic (e.g., checks `cleaned_data[f.name] is not None` instead of field.empty_values, or checks truthiness which fails for False/0)
scale.4: Correctly checks against the form field's empty_values (or equivalent) to distinguish meaningful from empty cleaned_data, preserving defaults for empty values
scale.5: All of level 4 plus validates both scenarios: (a) empty cleaned_data preserves model default, (b) meaningful cleaned_data overrides default, with explicit test cases for both

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Correct Fix Implementation in construct_instance for cleaned_data Precedence
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory implements the correct fix in `construct_instance` (django/forms/models.py ~line 52) to allow `cleaned_data` to override model field defaults. The fix must modify the condition that currently skips fields with defaults when `value_omitted_from_data` returns True, by adding a check that the field is NOT in `cleaned_data` before skipping. Excellent continuations will show the exact edit: changing `if f.has_default() and form[f.name].field.widget.value_omitted_from_data(...):` to `if f.has_default() and form[f.name].field.widget.value_omitted_from_data(...) and f.name not in cleaned_data:` (or equivalent logic that preserves the cleaned_data value).

metadata.key_edit_location: Line ~52, the condition checking f.has_default() and value_omitted_from_data
metadata.required_logic: Skip default only if field has default AND value omitted from data AND field not in cleaned_data
metadata.preserve_behavior: Checkbox inputs (value_omitted_from_data for unchecked checkboxes) should still work correctly
metadata.judge_focus: Whether the edit correctly allows cleaned_data to take precedence over model defaults while preserving existing behavior for fields not explicitly set in clean()

scale.1: No fix attempted, or fix applied to wrong file/function
scale.2: Fix attempted but modifies unrelated logic (e.g., changes widget behavior, modifies clean() method instead of construct_instance)
scale.3: Fix modifies construct_instance but the condition is incorrect - e.g., removes the default check entirely, or checks the wrong variable, or breaks the checkbox exception
scale.4: Fix correctly adds `f.name not in cleaned_data` check (or equivalent) to the existing condition in construct_instance, preserving checkbox handling and default behavior for fields not in cleaned_data
scale.5: Fix is correct AND the trajectory validates it with the reproduction test, showing the field now takes the cleaned_data value instead of the default

experiences.title: Cross-Path Bug Discovery Outweighs Same-Path Test Volume in Multi-Path Fix Validation
experiences.description: When an issue affects two distinct code paths and a fix addresses only one, a continuation that tests the unfixed path and discovers it still fails provides stronger validation evidence than one that runs multiple passing tests on the already-fixed path. Do not let the quantity of successful same-path tests obscure the diagnostic value of a cross-path failure discovery or an edge case crash.
experiences.context: A seaborn legend offset issue where large numbers (order 1E6) show wrong legend labels because the ScalarFormatter offset is not applied. The issue explicitly states both so.Plot (via scales.py Continuous._legend) and sns.scatterplot (via utils.py locator_to_legend_entries) are affected. Fixes that only modify scales.py leave the scatterplot path unfixed. Edge cases include negative values (Unicode minus '−' vs ASCII '-' causing float() conversion failure) and math text format offsets (LaTeX like '$\times\mathdefault{10^{6}}$' vs '1e6').
experiences.experience:
Activation: When an issue report identifies multiple affected APIs or code paths and a continuation's fix only addresses one path.

Positive evidence: A continuation that tests the unfixed code path and discovers it still produces wrong output demonstrates that the fix is incomplete. For example, testing sns.scatterplot and finding legend labels show '3.0, 3.6, 4.2, 4.8, 5.4, 6.0' instead of true values like '3000000' is strong validation evidence that the scales.py-only fix is incomplete. Similarly, discovering that negative values produce labels with Unicode minus ('−6' instead of '-6000000.0') and crash with 'ValueError: could not convert string to float: −6' reveals an edge case the fix does not handle.

Contradictory evidence: A continuation may show multiple successful test scenarios on the fixed path — so.Plot with large numbers producing labels ['3000000.0', '4000000.0', '5000000.0', '6000000.0'], additive offset cases producing correct absolute labels, and small number cases all passing. While this demonstrates the fix works for the tested path, it does not validate the unfixed path and should not be scored higher than a continuation that discovered the cross-path failure or edge case crash.

Close-looking exclusions: A continuation that begins testing the second code path but whose test output is truncated or not visible in the paused state should not be credited for cross-path validation — only visible test results count. A continuation whose test attempts fail with API errors (e.g., 'AttributeError: Plotter object has no attribute get_axes' or 'Legend contents: None') has not validated anything regardless of test intent. A continuation that identifies the second code path location (e.g., finds locator_to_legend_entries in utils.py) but does not apply a fix there has not completed the fix.
