experiences.context: A Django JSONField bug where has_key/has_keys/has_any_keys fail for numeric keys on SQLite. The fix adds a force_string_keys parameter to compile_json_path. Multiple continuations attempt to validate by running tests but all fail to configure the test environment. One continuation (s04) shows the modified function signature via grep, another (s00) shows only ls/find and a failing django test command with no patch visible, and a third (s06) shows the original function then applies a sed fix at the very last step.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When scoring a validation rubric and every visible branch prefix shows failing test commands (nonzero returncodes, tracebacks), check whether any branch displays the modified source code in grep/sed/cat output before ranking by path usage.

Positive evidence: A branch whose grep/sed output shows a function signature with a newly added parameter (e.g., force_string_keys=False) that is absent from the original codebase is direct evidence the patch was applied to the checkout. This is stronger validation evidence than any number of failing test commands, because it confirms the modified source is the target of any future test run.

Contradictory evidence: A branch that uses /testbed-relative paths and invokes `python -m django test` but whose output is a traceback (RuntimeError: Model class doesn't declare an explicit app_label; ImproperlyConfigured: settings are not configured; ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests.settings') has NOT validated anything. Failed test-setup commands are evidence of validation failure, not validation success. Rank such a branch below a branch with visible modified source, even if the latter ran no tests.

Close-looking exclusions: Distinguish (a) a branch showing the ORIGINAL function signature (no new parameter) from (b) a branch showing the MODIFIED signature. Only (b) is patch evidence. A branch that applies a fix via sed -i at the very last step (s06) without any subsequent test execution or re-grep showing the result is weaker than a branch whose grep output already reflects the modification (s04), because the sed branch's success is asserted but not yet observed. Do not treat the mere invocation of `python -m django test` or `python -m pytest` as evidence; read the returncode and the output. A nonzero returncode with a traceback means the test did not run.

Abstention boundary: If no branch shows either modified source code or successful test execution in the visible prefix — e.g., all branches show only the original function and only failing test-setup commands — then validation correctness cannot be distinguished from the visible state and the event is unobservable. Do not infer a patch was applied from intent, worklog text, or path usage alone; require observable modified source or observable passing test output.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Target-Checkout Validation of JSONField Numeric Key Fix
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the continuation demonstrates the fix works by running a targeted reproduction/validation against the modified checkout (not an installed package), with clear evidence of correct targeting (checkout-relative paths, local imports, version matching the checkout) and successful execution of the reported test case: JsonFieldHasKeyTest.objects.filter(data__has_key='1111').count() == 1 (and similarly for has_keys/has_any_keys) on SQLite. Strong evidence includes a visible patch in the continuation's final output, commands run from the checkout root (/testbed) with checkout-relative file paths, and the numeric-key test passing. Weak evidence includes only test-infrastructure setup, validation against an installed Django package, or self-reported success without observable test execution covering the numeric-string key case.

metadata.oracle_test: JsonFieldHasKeyTest.objects.filter(data__has_key='1111').count() == 1 and similarly for has_keys/has_any_keys on SQLite
metadata.code_review: Verify commands use checkout-relative paths (e.g., /testbed/...), not installed-package paths (dist-packages/site-packages); verify test runner uses the modified source.
metadata.failure_mode: Validation runs against installed Django package, or only tests string keys ('foo') but not numeric-string keys ('1111'), or claims success without observable test execution.

scale.1: No target-checkout validation evidence: no reproduction/validation attempted, execution target unobservable, or no patch visible so any test output reflects the current codebase rather than the agent's changes.
scale.2: Weak evidence: agent intends local validation but targeting proof is incomplete (e.g., only environment setup, no test execution), or no patch visible yet but investigation uses checkout-relative paths.
scale.3: Moderate evidence: local targeting is plausible (e.g., commands run from /testbed with checkout-relative paths), but validation fails before exercising the numeric-key behavior or lacks version/path confirmation.
scale.4: Strong evidence: targeted reproduction runs against the modified checkout and covers the main numeric-key behavior (has_key/has_keys/has_any_keys with '1111'), though some secondary compatibility cases (MySQL, Oracle) remain untested.
scale.5: Very strong evidence: targeted reproduction/regression checks visibly run against the modified checkout, import/version/path evidence is clear, a visible patch exercises the changed code, and the checked behavior maps directly to the task-level invariant (numeric string keys work as object keys on SQLite, MySQL, and Oracle).

experiences.title: Require Visible Reproduction Error Output, Not Script Execution or Self-Reported Claims
experiences.description: When judging diagnosis-stage rubrics that require reproducing a specific bug, the judge must verify the exact error appears in visible terminal output. Running the reproduction script without error means the bug was NOT reproduced. Self-reported claims of reproduction without visible error output should not receive full credit.
experiences.context: Diagnosis stage for a scikit-learn FeatureUnion with pandas transform_output bug. The rubric requires reproducing the exact ValueError: Length mismatch and identifying the source file and function.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When scoring diagnosis rubrics that require reproducing a specific error.

Positive evidence: Visible terminal output showing the exact ValueError (e.g., 'Error: ValueError: Length mismatch: Expected axis has 4 elements, new values have 96 elements') combined with inspection of the relevant source file (_set_output.py) constitutes strong diagnosis evidence. A continuation that prints the exact error message from the issue and then reads the implicated source file should score at the top of the rubric.

Contradictory evidence: Running the reproduction script and getting successful output with NO error means the bug was NOT reproduced. If the pandas output shows correct transformation results (e.g., a DataFrame with dates and values) without any ValueError, the bug did not manifest. This should score at most level 1-2, not level 3+.

Close-looking exclusion: A THOUGHT that claims 'I have successfully reproduced the issue' without corresponding visible error output in the shown steps should not receive level 5 credit. The judge must verify actual error output in the terminal, not self-reported claims in reasoning text. If the reproduction output is not visible in the paused steps, the claim is unverified.

Reject misleading pattern: Do not conflate 'ran the reproduction script' with 'reproduced the bug.' If the script runs without the expected error, the bug was not reproduced regardless of whether the agent inspected source files afterward. A successful script execution with correct output is evidence of NON-reproduction, not diagnosis success.

Abstention boundary: When reproduction output is not visible in the paused state (e.g., it occurred in earlier unshown steps), do not award full credit based solely on THOUGHT claims. Require visible error output or explicit references to prior visible output. If no visible evidence of the error exists in the shown steps, cap the score at level 2.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Reproduces Bug and Identifies Root Cause Location
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The continuation successfully reproduces the exact reported bug (ValueError: Length mismatch when using FeatureUnion with pandas transform_output and an aggregating transformer) AND identifies the specific source file and function where the fix must be applied (sklearn/utils/_set_output.py, specifically _wrap_in_pandas_container or _wrap_data_with_container). This distinguishes continuations that have actionable diagnosis from those stuck on environment issues or those that found a pre-fixed version without understanding the mechanism.

metadata.judge_focus: Check for: (1) successful execution of the reproduction script showing the exact ValueError, (2) identification of sklearn/utils/_set_output.py as the relevant file, (3) identification of _wrap_in_pandas_container or _wrap_data_with_container as the function needing fix, (4) explanation of the row-count-mismatch mechanism
metadata.oracle_test: python test_issue.py should show 'Error: ValueError: Length mismatch: Expected axis has 4 elements, new values have 96 elements' for pandas output
metadata.failure_mode: environment_blocked_or_superficial_inspection

scale.1: Cannot run reproduction script due to environment/build issues; no bug reproduction or code inspection
scale.2: Runs reproduction but gets unrelated errors (import errors, build failures); no valid bug reproduction
scale.3: Successfully reproduces the exact ValueError: Length mismatch error, but has not located the responsible source code
scale.4: Successfully reproduces the bug AND identifies the relevant source file (sklearn/utils/_set_output.py) but has not pinpointed the exact function or mechanism
scale.5: Successfully reproduces the bug, identifies the exact function (_wrap_in_pandas_container or _wrap_data_with_container), and explains the mechanism (forcing input index onto output with different row count)

experiences.title: Separate false-negative reproduction from root-cause identification; calibrate criteria to visible stage
experiences.description: Use this when a bug report names a specific backend, version, or runtime condition and trajectories show reproduction attempts that may produce false-negative 'success' under mismatched conditions. The core failure mode is a rubric that conflates reproduction output or environment setup with root-cause identification, causing the judge to reward a trajectory that obtained a misleading 'success' over trajectories that actually investigated the failing code path. A second failure mode is a rubric that demands implementation details not yet visible in an exploration-stage prefix, yielding uninformative all-zero scores across all candidates.
experiences.context: Applies in SWE-agent diagnosis or exploration trajectories where the reported bug is environment- or backend-specific (e.g., a particular GUI backend, OS, or library version). The misleading case is when a continuation runs the reproduction script and sees a 'successful' or 'no error' output because it used a different backend or version than the bug report, then the judge treats that output as evidence of root-cause understanding or fix validation. Equally misleading is rewarding environment-setup commands (path manipulation, package installation, version checks) as if they were root-cause analysis. The judge must instead look at whether the trajectory recognizes the condition mismatch, attempts to match the reported environment, or investigates the actual code path where the unpicklable or unserializable reference originates.
experiences.experience: The previous rubric conflated root-cause identification with reproduction or validation success. That conflation inverts the evidence when the reproduction is a false negative: a trajectory that sees a pass output under a mismatched backend has not identified the root cause and may be worse than a trajectory that fails to reproduce but correctly investigates the source code. A better rubric should: (1) treat any 'success' output obtained under conditions that do not match the bug report as a false negative requiring further investigation, not as positive evidence; (2) explicitly decline to reward environment-setup commands as root-cause progress; (3) score root-cause evidence from reading the actual class or function where the reported unpicklable reference is stored, recognizing pickle-state customization patterns, or recognizing the backend or version mismatch; (4) calibrate scale anchors to what is visible at the current trajectory stage so that exploration-stage prefixes are not scored against implementation completeness they cannot yet show. When the visible prefix cannot distinguish whether a trajectory will reach the root cause, preserve uncertainty rather than assigning extreme scores.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Root-cause identification calibrated to reported conditions and visible stage
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Judge whether the trajectory identifies the actual source of the reported failure under the conditions named in the bug report, not whether it obtained a 'success' output that may be a false negative. Positive evidence includes recognizing that a 'successful' reproduction used a different backend or version than reported and is therefore inconclusive, attempting to match the reported environment, reading the class or function where the unpicklable or unserializable object reference is stored, identifying pickle-state customization patterns or existing pickle-safe mechanisms in the codebase, and connecting the stored object reference to the reported TypeError or serialization failure. Do not score environment-setup commands (path manipulation, pip install, version checks) as root-cause evidence. Do not anchor scale levels on implementation completeness when the visible prefix only shows exploration and no patch is visible.

metadata.activation: Bug report names a specific backend, version, OS, or runtime condition; trajectory shows reproduction attempts, environment setup, or source-code reading
positive_evidence: trajectory recognizes that a 'success' output used a mismatched backend or version and is a false negative
trajectory attempts to reproduce under the reported conditions, for example by trying the named backend
trajectory reads the class or function where the unpicklable reference is stored, such as a base class holding a canvas or backend object reference
trajectory identifies pickle-state customization patterns like __getstate__ or __setstate__ or existing pickle-safe callback mechanisms in the codebase
trajectory connects the stored object reference to the reported TypeError or serialization failure
contradictory_evidence: a pass or 'successful' output obtained with a different backend or version than the bug report names, presented as root-cause progress
environment-setup commands such as sys.path.insert, PYTHONPATH manipulation, pip install, or version checks scored as root-cause identification
trajectory does not question a 'success' result when the bug report says the operation should fail under the reported conditions
close_exclusions: do not reward reading test files or test exploration as root-cause identification if the trajectory does not connect the tests to the failing code path
do not penalize a trajectory that fails to reproduce due to environment limitations if it recognizes the mismatch and investigates the source code instead
do not treat 'cannot load backend' or import errors as negative evidence if the trajectory uses them to recognize the condition mismatch
do not score all candidates zero because implementation details are not yet visible; calibrate anchors to the exploration stage
metadata.abstention_boundary: When the visible prefix shows only early exploration and no trajectory has yet reached the root-cause code or recognized the condition mismatch, preserve uncertainty. Do not assign extreme high or low scores based solely on reproduction output or environment setup. Distinguish trajectories that are still progressing toward root cause from those that have stopped at a false-negative reproduction.

scale.1: No root-cause evidence: trajectory only runs reproduction or environment setup, obtains a false-negative 'success' under mismatched conditions, and does not question it or investigate source code.
scale.2: Trajectory runs reproduction and sees 'success' but does not investigate further, or only performs environment setup without reading the relevant source code.
scale.3: Trajectory recognizes the condition mismatch or begins reading the relevant source code such as the class holding the unpicklable reference, but has not yet connected it to the reported failure.
scale.4: Trajectory both recognizes the condition mismatch and reads the actual code path where the unpicklable or unserializable reference is stored, connecting it to the reported failure or identifying pickle-state customization needs.
scale.5: Trajectory fully identifies the root cause: recognizes false-negative reproduction, reads the exact class and attribute causing the failure, identifies the pickle-state customization pattern needed, and connects this to the reported error condition.

experiences.title: Reproduction and offset understanding without fix application is not root-cause-to-fix alignment
experiences.description: A continuation that reproduces the exact reported seaborn.objects scenario and demonstrates understanding of the ScalarFormatter offset mechanism but applies no patch to the actual fix location should not outscore a continuation that modifies the correct code location and demonstrates correct offset parsing and label correction. Reproduction validates the bug exists; it does not validate fix alignment.
experiences.context: In seaborn's ContinuousBase._setup (scales.py ~line 382), legend labels are set from format_ticks(locs) without applying formatter.get_offset(). The fix requires modifying this code to retrieve and apply the offset to each formatted label.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When comparing continuations where one reproduces the reported seaborn.objects plotting scenario and understands the ScalarFormatter offset (get_offset() returns '1e6', orderOfMagnitude 6) but has no patch (changed_files: None), while another applies a patch to scales.py with demonstrated offset parsing.

Positive evidence: A continuation that modifies scales.py (the actual fix location), tests offset parsing (e.g., '1e6' -> 1000000.0), and computes corrected labels (e.g., ['3000000.0', '3500000.0', ...]) shows strong root-cause-to-fix alignment. The presence of a patch at the exact fix location with correct offset parsing is the primary evidence for fix alignment.

Contradictory evidence: Running the exact reported code and confirming the bug (body_mass_mg range 2.7M-6.3M, legend shows simplified values) is evidence for validation, not for fix alignment. Understanding get_offset() and orderOfMagnitude without applying a fix does not close the root-cause-to-fix gap. A continuation with no patch has not demonstrated fix alignment regardless of how well it understands the mechanism. Do not use reproduction of the reported scenario and offset mechanism understanding as proxies for root-cause-to-fix alignment.

Close-looking exclusions: (1) Testing ScalarFormatter in isolation without connecting to scales.py does not show fix alignment even with offset understanding. (2) Proposing string concatenation (label + offset producing '3.01e6') is an incorrect fix approach that produces wrong values, not correct offset application. (3) Finding the _legend code but only exploring _legend references without modifying the fix location has not demonstrated fix alignment.

Abstention boundary: If a continuation applies a patch to the correct fix location but no visible evidence shows what the patch does (no offset parsing test, no label computation, no diff content visible), then fix alignment cannot be verified from visible evidence and this experience does not apply. Here, the patched continuation's visible evidence includes offset parsing and label computation, so the distinction is observable.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Root-Cause-to-Fix Alignment for ScalarFormatter Offset in Legend
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the agent's investigation or fix correctly targets the ScalarFormatter offset handling in the legend label generation. The root cause is that `ContinuousBase._setup` (or `Continuous._setup`) creates legend labels directly from `axis.major.formatter.format_ticks(locs)` without applying the formatter's offset (available via `formatter.get_offset()`). An excellent continuation either: (a) identifies this exact code location and explains why the offset must be applied to each label, or (b) implements a fix that retrieves the offset and correctly combines it with the formatted labels (e.g., by parsing the scientific notation offset and multiplying, or by prepending the offset string). A weak continuation either misses the offset mechanism entirely, focuses on unrelated formatter settings (rcParams), or proposes a fix at the wrong abstraction level (e.g., changing tick formatting globally instead of fixing legend label generation).

metadata.oracle_test: Create a plot with large values (1e6+), check if legend labels show actual values (e.g., 3000000) not offset values (e.g., 3.0)
metadata.code_review: Focus on seaborn/_core/scales.py ContinuousBase._setup method around line 382 where new._legend = list(locs), list(labels) is set
metadata.judge_focus: Does the continuation identify that formatter.get_offset() returns '1e6' and this must be applied to each formatted label? Does any fix correctly parse and apply this offset?
metadata.failure_mode: Fixes tick formatting instead of legend labels; ignores offset entirely; applies offset incorrectly (string concatenation vs numeric multiplication); changes rcParams instead of fixing the label generation

scale.1: No evidence of correct root-cause identification: continuation explores unrelated code, focuses on rcParams, or proposes fixes that don't address the offset-to-legend gap
scale.2: Weak evidence: continuation finds the legend creation code but doesn't connect it to ScalarFormatter offset, or mentions offset but doesn't trace to the exact fix location
scale.3: Moderate evidence: continuation identifies the _setup method and knows offset exists, but fix approach is unclear or incomplete (e.g., only string prepending without parsing)
scale.4: Strong evidence: continuation correctly identifies the exact fix location, explains the offset mechanism, and proposes or implements a fix that retrieves and applies the offset to legend labels
scale.5: Strongest evidence: continuation implements a verified fix that correctly parses formatter.get_offset() (e.g., '1e6' -> 1000000.0) and applies it to each label, producing correct legend values for large ranges

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation Against Reported Scenario
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the continuation validates its diagnosis or fix against the exact user-reported scenario: creating a seaborn.objects Plot with point sizes in the millions (body_mass_mg) and verifying the legend shows correct values (e.g., 3,000,000) not offset-simplified values (e.g., 3.0). An excellent continuation either: (a) runs the reported code and confirms the legend bug visually or programmatically, or (b) applies a fix and then runs the reported code to confirm the legend now shows correct values. A weak continuation only tests ScalarFormatter in isolation, uses synthetic data, tests against a different code path (e.g., scatterplot without verifying the objects interface), or applies a patch without any regression test matching the original report.

metadata.oracle_test: Run the exact user code: so.Plot(penguins, x='bill_length_mm', y='bill_depth_mm', color='species', pointsize='body_mass_mg').add(so.Dot()) and check legend labels
metadata.code_review: Look for execution of the reported plotting code, not just formatter unit tests
metadata.judge_focus: Does the continuation run the actual seaborn.objects code from the issue and verify legend values? For fixes, does it re-run the same code to confirm correction?
metadata.failure_mode: Only tests formatter.get_offset() in isolation; uses synthetic random data; tests scatterplot but not objects interface; applies patch without running the reported scenario; concludes bug is fixed without target-checkout validation

scale.1: No validation: continuation only explores code or tests formatter in isolation, never runs the reported seaborn.objects plotting code
scale.2: Weak validation: continuation runs some plotting code but not the exact reported scenario (e.g., different data, different API, or only checks axis ticks not legend)
scale.3: Moderate validation: continuation runs the reported code and observes the bug (wrong legend values) but does not verify a fix, or verifies a fix but with different test data
scale.4: Strong validation: continuation runs the exact reported code, observes the bug, and if a fix is applied, re-runs the exact same code to confirm legend shows correct values (e.g., 3000000 not 3.0)
scale.5: Strongest validation: continuation runs the exact reported scenario, confirms the bug, implements a fix, re-runs the exact scenario to confirm correct legend values, and ideally adds a regression test matching the report

experiences.title: Submitted Patch Content Must Match Target File—Not Just Intermediate Git Diffs
experiences.description: When a continuation submits a final patch by displaying its content (e.g., cat /tmp/patch.txt), the judge must verify the diff header in the displayed output references the expected target file. A continuation can show correct code changes in git diff and pass all tests in intermediate steps, but the patch file submitted may contain a diff for a completely unrelated file. The judge must not credit intermediate evidence when the final submission contains a patch for a different file.
experiences.context: In a bug fix task for sklearn's _wrap_in_pandas_container function in sklearn/utils/_set_output.py, continuations add a RangeIndex check before overwriting the output DataFrame's index. Multiple continuations show correct git diffs and pass reproduction and edge case tests. One continuation's final submission step displays a diff for an unrelated module (sympy/printing/mathml.py) instead of the target file (sklearn/utils/_set_output.py), indicating the patch file was overwritten or contains stale content.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When a continuation reaches a submission step that displays patch content (e.g., 'echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat /tmp/patch.txt'), examine the diff header in the displayed output to verify it references the expected target file.

Positive evidence: Git diffs showing the correct fix in the target file, reproduction scripts passing, and edge case tests passing are positive indicators that the fix is correct in the working tree. A sophisticated fix using isinstance(index, pd.RangeIndex) checks demonstrates strong fix quality.

Contradictory evidence: If the submission step's cat output shows a diff header referencing a different file path (e.g., 'diff --git a/sympy/printing/mathml.py' when the target is 'sklearn/utils/_set_output.py'), the submitted patch does not contain the fix. This contradicts all intermediate evidence regardless of how many tests passed or how sophisticated the git diff appeared. The patch file may have been overwritten by another process or contain stale content from a prior operation.

Close-looking exclusions: Verify the file path in the diff header of the submitted patch matches the target file. A diff for 'a/sympy/printing/mathml.py' is not equivalent to a diff for 'a/sklearn/utils/_set_output.py' even if both show code changes. Do not assume the patch file content matches the git diff just because both were displayed in the trajectory. The git diff reflects the working tree state; the patch file is what gets submitted and may differ.

Abstention boundary: If the submission step does not display patch content, or if the displayed content is truncated such that the diff header (the 'diff --git a/...' line) is not visible, do not credit or penalize based on submission content alone—rely on other visible evidence such as git diff and test results. If no submission step is visible (continuation is paused), evaluate based on available evidence only.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Validation Thoroughness: Targeted Contract Verification and Regression Coverage
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluates whether the continuation validates the fix with evidence that exercises the exact reported failure scenario (FeatureUnion + pandas output + aggregation transformer) AND covers critical edge cases (empty DataFrames, custom indices, numpy array inputs, MultiIndex, transformers that preserve vs change row count) AND runs existing sklearn regression test suites (test_set_output.py, test_pipeline.py, test_column_transformer.py) to ensure no regressions. Superior continuations demonstrate all three validation layers; weaker ones only run the minimal reproduction script.

metadata.judge_focus: Look for explicit test commands (pytest, python test scripts) and their outputs in the continuation's visible steps. Check for: (1) original issue reproduction script execution, (2) edge case test scripts covering empty DataFrame, custom index preservation, numpy array input, MultiIndex, mixed row counts, (3) pytest execution on sklearn/utils/tests/test_set_output.py, sklearn/tests/test_pipeline.py, sklearn/compose/tests/test_column_transformer.py with pass/fail results. Do not credit mere claims of testing without visible command output.
metadata.failure_mode: validation_gap_regression_risk
metadata.oracle_test: Continuation should show: python test_issue.py (original bug fixed), python test_edge_cases.py (comprehensive edge cases pass), pytest sklearn/utils/tests/test_set_output.py (14 passed), pytest sklearn/tests/test_pipeline.py (87 passed), pytest sklearn/compose/tests/test_column_transformer.py (183 passed)

scale.1: Only runs the original reproduction script (test_issue.py) with no additional validation; no edge case testing, no regression suite execution
scale.2: Runs reproduction script plus a few ad-hoc checks but misses key edge cases (e.g., empty DataFrame, custom index preservation, numpy array path) and does not run existing sklearn test suites
scale.3: Runs reproduction script and covers most critical edge cases (aggregation, same-row-count with custom index, numpy array input) but does not run existing sklearn test suites for regression coverage
scale.4: Runs reproduction script, comprehensive edge cases (empty DataFrame, MultiIndex, custom index preservation, numpy array, mixed row counts in FeatureUnion), AND runs at least one existing sklearn test suite (test_set_output.py or test_pipeline.py or test_column_transformer.py) with all tests passing
scale.5: Runs reproduction script, exhaustive edge cases covering all code paths in _wrap_in_pandas_container (DataFrame, Series, numpy array; default vs custom index; length match vs mismatch; empty; MultiIndex), AND runs multiple existing sklearn test suites (test_set_output.py, test_pipeline.py, test_column_transformer.py) with all tests passing, demonstrating full regression safety

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fix Sophistication: Dual Protection of Transformer Semantic Index
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The fix intelligently preserves the transformer's meaningful output index in TWO scenarios: (1) when aggregation changes row count (length mismatch), AND (2) when row count matches but the transformer provides a semantic non-RangeIndex index (e.g., grouped dates, custom labels). The superior fix checks `isinstance(data_to_wrap.index, pd.RangeIndex)` before overwriting, rather than only checking length equality. This prevents silent loss of semantic index information in both aggregation and non-aggregation transformers.

metadata.judge_focus: Check if _wrap_in_pandas_container uses `isinstance(data_to_wrap.index, pd.RangeIndex)` or equivalent semantic-index detection, not just length comparison. Verify fix handles both DataFrame and numpy array code paths.
metadata.failure_mode: semantic_index_overwrite_when_lengths_match
metadata.oracle_test: Transformer returning DataFrame with custom index (e.g., ['a','b','c']) and same row count as input should preserve ['a','b','c'] index under pandas output, not be overwritten by input's index

scale.1: Fix only checks length match; overwrites transformer's index with input's index whenever lengths match, losing semantic index in non-aggregation cases
scale.2: Fix checks length match but has bugs in index preservation logic (e.g., wrong condition, crashes on numpy arrays)
scale.3: Fix correctly preserves semantic index when lengths differ (aggregation), but still overwrites meaningful index when lengths match
scale.4: Fix uses RangeIndex check to preserve semantic index in both aggregation and non-aggregation cases; handles DataFrame and numpy array inputs correctly
scale.5: Fix implements clean dual-protection: preserves transformer's index whenever it's not a default RangeIndex, regardless of length match; handles all input types (DataFrame, Series, numpy array); passes all existing tests without regression

experiences.title: Require visible source inspection of the root-cause mechanism before awarding root-cause-identification scores
experiences.description: Retrieve when scoring diagnostic investigation trajectories against rubrics whose mid-to-high levels require identifying a specific code mechanism as the root cause, especially when some trajectories attempt reproduction setup while others inspect the actual source.
experiences.context: Applies when a rubric scale ties score levels to progressively deeper source-code investigation: locating an error message, finding a data structure, identifying the order-sensitive mechanism, and creating a reproduction. A common evidence-reading error is to award a trajectory a mid-to-high score because it is attempting to run a reproduction test, without verifying that the trajectory has actually inspected the specific root-cause code. At a visible cutoff, a trajectory may be cycling through dependency installation or import-error resolution for its reproducer while having shown no commands or output that inspect the root-cause mechanism. Meanwhile, other trajectories may have already displayed the relevant source but received lower scores. The judge must read which specific source the trajectory has actually inspected and map that to the rubric level, not infer root-cause identification from the mere existence of a test file or reproduction attempt.
experiences.experience: When scoring diagnostic investigation, do not award a score at or above the rubric level that requires 'identified the root-cause mechanism' unless the visible trajectory contains commands or output that inspect that specific mechanism (e.g., grep/sed/cat output showing the parent_links dictionary construction or the metaclass field-collection logic). A trajectory that is installing dependencies, resolving import errors, or creating/running a reproducer without prior source inspection of the mechanism has not yet reached that rubric level; score it at or below the level for 'found error message location only' or 'no investigation of the mechanism,' depending on what source it has actually viewed. Conversely, trajectories that have displayed the root-cause data structure in source but have not yet connected it to the order dependency should be scored at the intermediate level for 'found the data structure but hasn't connected the mechanism,' not below trajectories that have not inspected the code at all. Close-looking exclusion: locating the error message in the file that raises it is not equivalent to identifying the root-cause mechanism in the metaclass that populates the data structure; the former corresponds to the lowest rubric level. Abstain from awarding the top score when the visible prefix is too short to confirm both root-cause identification and reproduction, even if a test file exists on disk.

experiences.title: Gate full credit on real-code bytes bypass in shared _encode_params, not simulated validation
experiences.description: Retrieve when the task concerns a binary request body failing because `_encode_params` sends bytes through `to_native_string`, and the visible trajectory shows `_encode_params` is a shared helper used from both URL-parameter preparation and body-data preparation. The judge must require visible evidence that the actual modified code makes raw bytes bypass native-string decoding before any broader string condition catches them, while preserving the URL-parameter use of the same helper. Do not give full credit merely because the agent reproduces the error, states the right intention, or tests a locally redefined stand-in function.
experiences.context: Activation evidence in the paused view includes `_encode_params` in `models.py`, `to_native_string` decoding bytes with the default ASCII behavior, `compat.py` showing that `basestring`/string checks include bytes on Python 3, and grep output showing `_encode_params` called in different contexts such as `params` and request-body `data`. This card is most important after a continuation edits `models.py` with a textual replacement script or abbreviated command output and then validates using a separate Python snippet that reimplements `_encode_params` logic instead of importing/executing the actual modified function.
experiences.experience:
For this task, full-credit rubrics need a hard correctness gate: the visible patch or actual executed code must show that binary body bytes are not passed to `to_native_string`. Equivalent implementations are valid, but bytes must escape native-string decoding before they can be matched by a broad condition such as `isinstance(data, (str, bytes))` or compatibility aliases that include bytes. Because `_encode_params` is also used for URL parameters, the rubric should also require evidence that the change does not collapse the URL-encoding path for iterable/key-value parameters or ordinary text strings.

Positive evidence: the trajectory inspects the real `_encode_params` branch after editing, or imports/runs the actual modified function; the code path clearly returns/preserves byte payloads without ASCII decoding; string inputs still follow the intended native-string behavior; iterable/key-value parameters still reach `urlencode`; and the agent recognizes the separate `params` and body-data call sites visible from grep.

Contradictory evidence: the only validation is a freshly defined local `_encode_params` or pseudocode copy; the actual patched file is not shown after a replacement script; a bytes-specific branch appears after a broader `(str, bytes)`/`basestring` branch and is therefore unreachable; the fix changes the encoding to UTF-8 and decodes arbitrary body bytes into text; or the trajectory focuses on unrelated interpreter compatibility imports without proving the binary-body path is fixed.

Close-looking exclusions: reproducing the UnicodeDecodeError is not evidence of a correct fix. A simulated unit snippet that demonstrates desired logic is not evidence that the repository code contains that logic. A grep showing call sites is useful exploration but not enough unless the continuation also preserves both call-site contexts. A patch summary saying `models.py` changed is not enough when the crucial branch ordering is hidden or truncated.

Abstention boundary: if the paused view does not reveal the actual edited `_encode_params` branch ordering and does not show execution of the actual modified function, preserve uncertainty and avoid maximum scores. Score based on visible evidence only; do not assume a text replacement did what the agent intended.

experiences.title: Judge the end-to-end ModelForm construction path, not isolated empty-label terminology
experiences.description: For issues where a model-backed form using a radio-style widget renders an unwanted blank foreign-key choice even though the model field has blank=False, judge the continuation by whether it follows the actual construction and final rendering path from the ModelForm definition to the produced choices. Do not give high credit merely because the continuation mentions the semantically attractive idea of propagating blank, or because it greps a related field's formfield() method. The strongest evidence is concrete tracing or tests showing how the model field's blank setting, the ModelForm widget override, the generated ModelChoiceField, and the final RadioSelect choices interact while preserving existing behavior for other widgets and blank=True cases.
experiences.context: The observable behavior is a rendered radio group for a model foreign key: when blank is not a valid model value, the radio choices should not include or preselect a blank value; when blank is valid or when a select-style widget conventionally uses an empty option, existing behavior must be preserved. The relevant path starts in ModelForm field construction: Meta.widgets and model fields are processed by the ModelForm machinery, each model field builds a form field, and the resulting ModelChoiceField determines its empty_label/choices before rendering. A fix that only changes templates, or only suppresses a yielded choice inside a choice iterator based on widget type and required status, can match the visual symptom while breaking cleaning, choice consistency, or non-radio cases.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Use this rule when the visible work concerns a ModelForm/model-field choice rendered with a radio-style widget and the bug is about whether a blank option appears when the model field disallows blank.

Primary positive evidence: Prefer continuations that inspect or reason through the end-to-end ModelForm construction path: ModelForm metaclass/base-form setup, fields_for_model or equivalent model-field-to-form-field creation, the application of Meta.widgets, the model field's formfield() call, and ModelChoiceField empty_label/choice handling. At an early exploratory stage, a focused attempt to trace this ModelForm path is stronger evidence than jumping directly to a single lower-level method. Highest credit requires an explicit connection from model-field blank plus the supplied radio widget to the final form field choices, or a test/assertion of the rendered final state such as no blank radio input being present or checked for blank=False.

Required final-state checks for strong credit: A proposed design or patch should be judged by observable outcomes, not naming alone. Reward evidence that it preserves select-widget blank-option conventions, allows blank=True model fields to keep a blank choice where appropriate, keeps required-field cleaning/validation semantics intact, and avoids changing unrelated choice iteration behavior. Equivalent implementations are valid if these final states hold; do not require a particular file or exact patch shape.

Weak or misleading proxies: Do not assign high scores for merely grepping or opening ForeignKey.formfield, ModelChoiceField, or empty_label code without showing how the ModelForm widget override and model-field blank value reach the final choices. Do not reward multiple restatements of 'propagate blank' unless backed by direct code-path evidence or final-state behavior. Isolated exploration of widget templates, option HTML, generic render loops, or broad definition listings is at most neutral unless it is tied back to the ModelForm construction path.

Contradictory evidence: Strongly penalize continuations that frame the fix as detecting RadioSelect, input_type, or required status inside ModelChoiceIterator.__iter__ or another late choice-yielding/rendering layer to suppress the blank option. Such a continuation should not score above neutral on this issue even if it correctly observes that an empty_label is being yielded, because the visible symptom is not enough to establish a safe contract. Also penalize designs that use required alone as the source of truth for whether blank is a valid model selection.

Rubric guidance: Use balanced positive and negative criteria. Put substantial weight on direct ModelForm-path tracing and final rendered/validation behavior; put comparable negative weight on iterator/template/required-gated fixes. Avoid a pure positive rubric that lets any mention of formfield(), blank, or empty_label outrank better evidence of the complete construction path.

experiences.title: Retain reproduction-stage rubrics when all branches are pre-implementation
experiences.description: When every visible continuation is paused before implementation (zero target-file diff, no correct source edits), do not collapse the rubric portfolio to a single implementation-completeness rubric that demands source modifications and modified-source validation. That collapse assigns all branches the same floor score and destroys pairwise ranking. Explicitly forbid applying an 'implementation completeness should dominate' rule when no branch has reached implementation. Retain at least one rubric that scores observable reproduction and evidence-gathering behavior so branches can be differentiated by what they actually accomplished during exploration.
experiences.context: Applies to multi-branch SWE-agent code-repair trajectories scored at a paused, pre-implementation snapshot. The harmful pattern is a retrieved or updated rule stating 'implementation completeness should dominate' applied uniformly when all branches are still exploring, reproducing, or setting up the environment. A portfolio that includes reproduction and evidence-gathering rubrics discriminates correctly at this stage; an implementation-only rubric produces an uninformative tie at the floor.
experiences.experience:
Activation: All visible continuations show zero diff on the target file (or only wrong-file edits) and the trajectory is paused before any correct implementation; the judge must rank exploratory branches against each other.

Positive evidence to score in the retained reproduction/evidence rubric: (1) created a standalone reproduction script that exercises the reported error path; (2) resolved environment, import, or dependency errors and reached the actual failure rather than a setup crash; (3) reproduced the exact reported exception or failure mode; (4) compared against a working reference path — a sibling API, format, or code path that already supports the requested feature — to show the expected output; (5) identified the existing codebase pattern or class that the fix should follow, with specific reference to the relevant methods or attributes.

Contradictory evidence — do NOT demand at this stage: requiring visible target-file edits when no branch has made them; requiring modified-source test validation against a patched codebase when no patch exists; scoring every branch at the floor solely because implementation is incomplete.

Close-looking exclusions: 'No implementation yet' is not equivalent to 'no progress' — reproduction, environment setup, and pattern identification are real, rankable evidence and must not be conflated with zero achievement. Do not reward generic or repetitive grep/cat/sed searches that add no new information after the relevant files are already located; the reproduction rubric should still penalize pure looping. Edits to wrong or unrelated files are negative evidence (misdirected implementation), not neutral. A branch that hits an environment error and stops without reaching the reported failure is not equivalent to one that resolved the error and reproduced the failure.

Abstention boundary: If at least one branch has begun correct target-file edits, implementation-completeness rubrics may be added alongside reproduction rubrics — do not exclude them, and weight them appropriately for the implementing branches. If the visible prefix cannot distinguish whether a branch is about to implement or is stuck in exploration, preserve uncertainty: rank via the reproduction/evidence rubric and leave implementation-quality scores uncertain rather than forcing a uniform floor. Do not infer implementation quality from exploration alone, and do not infer exploration failure from the absence of edits when the snapshot is paused before implementation.

experiences.title: Require Visible Patch Evidence Before Scoring Code-Fix Rubrics
experiences.description: When no patch is visible in a paused state, code-fix rubrics must not receive positive scores for source-file reading alone, and fix-quality penalties must not be inferred from reproduction output that reflects the current codebase rather than the agent's changes.
experiences.context: Judges evaluating code-fix rubrics at paused states may encounter agents that have investigated the codebase (read files, run reproductions) but have not yet written a patch. The judge must distinguish investigation from modification. A visible diff is the only reliable evidence of a code fix; reading files and running scripts are investigation. Reproduction output when no patch exists reflects the current codebase's behavior, not the agent's modifications.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when scoring code-fix rubrics at a paused state. First check the agent summary fields: changed_files, current_patch_chars, and diff_stat. If changed_files is None or empty and current_patch_chars is 0, no patch has been written.

Positive Evidence (supports scoring above neutral on code-fix rubrics):
- changed_files lists the relevant source file under the codebase being tested
- current_patch_chars > 0 with visible patch content modifying the relevant logic
- Non-empty diff_stat showing changes to the function or file named in the rubric

Contradictory Evidence (prevents positive scores on code-fix rubrics):
- changed_files is None or empty and current_patch_chars is 0 — no fix has been applied
- The trajectory contains only read commands (grep, sed, cat, head) without any file write or patch operation
- The agent reads from installed-package paths (e.g., /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/...) rather than the source tree under test — this investigates the deployed package, not the codebase to be fixed
- No reproduction was run, or reproduction failed due to environment issues before any output was observed

Close-Looking Exclusions:
- A reproduction script that succeeds and shows correct output is NOT evidence of a code fix when current_patch_chars is 0. The output reflects the currently installed or built codebase, not the agent's patch. Do not treat successful reproduction output as evidence that the agent has fixed the issue.
- Describing the root cause or proposing a solution in natural language is NOT evidence of a fix. Understanding is necessary but not sufficient for a code-fix rubric.
- Reading the exact function that needs modification is NOT evidence of having modified it.
- An untracked reproduction script appearing in untracked_files but not changed_files is NOT a code fix to the source tree.
- An agent reading the installed package at /usr/local/lib/... rather than the source tree is investigating the deployed code, not fixing the codebase under test.

Forbidden Behaviors:
- Do not award positive scores on code-fix rubrics when changed_files is None and current_patch_chars is 0, regardless of how many relevant source files were read or how accurately the root cause was described.
- Do not apply maximum negative penalties on fix-quality rubrics based on reproduction output when no patch exists. Reproduction output shows current codebase behavior, not the agent's fix. If the reproduction output shows correct behavior (e.g., a semantic index preserved), this directly contradicts a negative fix-quality penalty.
- Do not infer a fix from the agent reading the relevant function, describing the problem, or running a reproduction.

Abstention Boundary:
- When no patch is visible, code-fix rubrics should receive neutral scores. The visible prefix cannot distinguish agents that will eventually produce a correct fix from those that will not. Preserve this uncertainty rather than resolving it with extreme positive or negative scores.
- If reproduction output is available but no patch exists, use it only to assess investigation depth and problem understanding, not fix quality.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fix Applied at Root Cause in Shared Utility
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The fix addresses the root cause in the generic `_wrap_in_pandas_container` utility function rather than patching only `FeatureUnion`. This ensures all meta-estimators (FeatureUnion, ColumnTransformer, Pipeline) and any future composition utilities automatically benefit from the correct row-count-mismatch handling without duplicating logic.

metadata.judge_focus: Verify the change is in sklearn/utils/_set_output.py (_wrap_in_pandas_container or _wrap_data_with_container) not in sklearn/pipeline.py (FeatureUnion.transform). Check that ColumnTransformer and Pipeline also work with aggregating transformers under pandas output.
metadata.failure_mode: narrow_fix_in_feature_union_only
metadata.oracle_test: ColumnTransformer([('agg', MyTransformer(), ['value', 'date'])]).fit_transform(data) with pandas output should also work without length mismatch error

scale.1: Fix only patches FeatureUnion.transform; ColumnTransformer and Pipeline still fail with aggregating transformers under pandas output
scale.2: Fix patches FeatureUnion and one other meta-estimator but misses others; logic duplicated across files
scale.3: Fix in _wrap_in_pandas_container but with FeatureUnion-specific conditional logic that doesn't generalize cleanly
scale.4: Fix in _wrap_in_pandas_container with general row-count-mismatch detection that works for all meta-estimators
scale.5: Fix in _wrap_data_with_container or _wrap_in_pandas_container with clean, general logic; all meta-estimators (FeatureUnion, ColumnTransformer, Pipeline) pass aggregating transformer tests; no duplicated logic; existing tests pass

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Handles Transformer Output Row Count Mismatch
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The fix correctly handles cases where a transformer's output has a different number of rows than its input (e.g., aggregation via groupby). When transform_output='pandas', the wrapping logic should detect row count mismatch and avoid forcing the original input's index onto the aggregated output, instead preserving the transformer's natural index or creating a default RangeIndex.

metadata.failure_mode: index_length_mismatch_after_aggregation
metadata.judge_focus: Check if _wrap_in_pandas_container or FeatureUnion's output handling detects len(output) != len(input) and skips index transfer in that case
metadata.oracle_test: make_union(MyTransformer()).fit_transform(data) with set_config(transform_output='pandas') should return DataFrame with 4 rows (one per date) not raise ValueError

scale.1: Fix does not address row count mismatch; still tries to force original index onto aggregated output
scale.2: Fix attempts to handle mismatch but introduces new bugs (e.g., wrong index, broken metadata)
scale.3: Fix detects row count mismatch in simple cases but fails for FeatureUnion with multiple transformers
scale.4: Fix correctly handles row count mismatch for single transformer and FeatureUnion, preserves transformer's natural index when available
scale.5: Fix robustly handles all aggregation scenarios: single transformer, FeatureUnion, ColumnTransformer; preserves semantic index from transformer output; falls back to RangeIndex only when necessary; passes all existing tests

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Discards Transformer's Semantic Output Index
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The fix discards the transformer's meaningful output index (e.g., grouped dates from a groupby operation) and replaces it with a generic RangeIndex, even when the transformer's output already has a correct, semantic index that differs from the input index only in length. This loses valuable semantic information that the transformer intentionally produced.

metadata.failure_mode: semantic_index_loss
metadata.judge_focus: Check if the fix preserves the transformer's output.index when len(output) != len(input) but output.index is already meaningful (e.g., the grouped dates), rather than unconditionally substituting RangeIndex
metadata.oracle_test: make_union(MyTransformer()).fit_transform(data) with pandas output should have index equal to the 4 unique dates from the groupby, not RangeIndex(4)

scale.1: Fix preserves transformer's output index when it exists and is meaningful; only falls back to RangeIndex when transformer returns numpy array or index-less object
scale.2: Fix mostly preserves semantic index but has edge cases where it incorrectly substitutes RangeIndex
scale.3: Fix sometimes preserves semantic index but often defaults to RangeIndex even when transformer provides a meaningful index
scale.4: Fix frequently discards meaningful transformer index in favor of RangeIndex, losing semantic information
scale.5: Fix unconditionally replaces any non-matching index with RangeIndex, completely discarding transformer's semantic output index

experiences.title: Redundant Testing Rubrics Amplify Proxy Validation Over Targeted Fix Verification
experiences.description: When a rubric set contains multiple rubrics that reward overlapping testing and validation activities, their combined weight can cause a continuation that performs broad but non-targeted testing to outscore one that performs targeted verification of the specific behavior the fix is meant to correct. The judge must ensure that overlapping testing rubrics do not collectively overshadow rubrics measuring actual fix correctness, and that a continuation's score reflects the relevance of its testing to the fix, not merely the quantity of test commands executed.
experiences.context: Software engineering evaluation often assesses testing discipline through multiple rubrics: running existing test suites, exercising specific test commands, running extended suites, verifying behavioral contracts, and isolating pre-existing failures. While each appears distinct, they frequently overlap in practice—a continuation running the project test suite and exercising specific commands both validate 'did the agent verify the fix against tests.' When these rubrics are weighted and summed, a continuation performing broad testing accumulates credit across all overlapping rubrics, inflating its score relative to a continuation that writes a targeted test for the specific behavior the fix addresses. Do not create multiple rubrics that all reward the same underlying testing activity; if rubrics overlap, consolidate them or reduce individual weights so their combined weight does not exceed rubrics measuring fix correctness.
experiences.experience:
Activation: Apply when two or more rubrics in the set measure related testing or validation activities such that broad testing would score across multiple rubrics while targeted testing of the fix's specific behavior scores on fewer rubrics. Check whether the combined weight of testing rubrics exceeds the weight of fix-correctness rubrics.

Positive evidence: A continuation that writes and runs a test verifying the specific behavior the fix corrects (e.g., the exact error path that was broken, the specific distinction the fix introduces) demonstrates higher-quality validation than one that merely runs existing test suites without targeting the fix behavior. When testing rubrics overlap, the continuation testing the specific distinguishing behavior should not score lower than one running more commands without targeting the fix behavior. Consolidate overlapping testing rubrics mentally: if two rubrics both reward running test suites or exercising test commands, their combined weight should not exceed the weight of a rubric measuring fix correctness.

Contradictory evidence: Rubrics measuring genuinely distinct dimensions (fix implementation pattern, regression testing across unrelated modules, patch hygiene) are not redundant and retain independent weights. A continuation performing both broad and targeted testing legitimately earns credit across all rubrics—do not penalize thoroughness. If the testing rubrics measure different stages of validation (e.g., one measures reproduction before the fix, another measures confirmation after), they are not redundant.

Close-looking exclusions: 'Exercising specific test commands' and 'running extended test suites' are related but not identical; however, a continuation hitting both accumulates overlapping credit—adjust scoring expectations so the combined credit does not dwarf targeted fix verification. 'Verifying a behavioral distinction' (e.g., CLI vs programmatic error handling) is more specific than 'running test commands'; the broader rubric's weight should not drown out the more specific one. Running the project's test suite and observing passes is useful validation but is not equivalent to testing the specific behavior the fix addresses—do not score them identically. A continuation that runs many test suites but never tests the specific error path the fix corrects has done broad proxy validation, not resolving verification.

Abstention boundary: If only one testing rubric exists or testing rubrics clearly measure non-overlapping dimensions, this rule does not apply. If visible evidence is insufficient to determine whether rubrics overlap (e.g., descriptions are vague or the testing activities are genuinely different stages), preserve uncertainty and do not adjust. Do not infer overlap from superficial keyword similarity alone; examine what each rubric actually measures in the context of the specific task. If the visible trajectory prefix is too short to distinguish whether a continuation's testing is targeted or broad, do not penalize or reward either way.

experiences.title: Guard-clause rubric alignment outweighs comprehensive validation when patch structure shows restructuring
experiences.description: When a rubric specifies an additive guard-clause fix and one continuation shows comprehensive validation of all contract behaviors but has a patch with significant deletions (restructuring), while another has a minimal additive patch matching the rubric but less comprehensive validation, the judge must weigh patch structure alignment with the rubric over validation output completeness. Restructured patches with deletions are more likely to break edge cases not covered by visible validation scripts.
experiences.context: Evaluating continuations for a RenameModel db_table noop fix where the rubric describes adding a guard clause checking original_attrs. Two continuations have patches: one with 3 insertions only (matching rubric's additive description) and one with 7 insertions/6 deletions (restructuring). The restructured patch shows comprehensive validation (table preserved, FK correct, M2M unaffected) while the additive patch's comprehensive test fails with a test infrastructure error.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When comparing continuations where one has comprehensive validation outputs but a restructured patch (insertions + deletions) and another has minimal validation but an additive-only patch matching the rubric's guard-clause description.

Positive evidence: A patch with insertions only (no deletions) that matches the rubric's description of 'adding a guard clause' or 'adding a conditional' is strong evidence of correct implementation, even if validation is less comprehensive. The diff_stat showing 0 deletions for a rubric that describes an additive change is a strong alignment signal. A 3-insertion patch for a guard-clause fix is the expected size.

Contradictory evidence: Comprehensive validation outputs showing all three contract behaviors working (table preserved, FK references correct table, M2M tables unaffected) can be misleading when the patch has significant deletions indicating restructuring rather than a simple guard clause addition. Validation scripts test specific cases that may pass even with a restructured patch that breaks edge cases not covered by the visible test scripts. Explicitly reject the pattern of using comprehensive validation outputs as the primary scoring signal when the patch structure (diff_stat with deletions) contradicts the rubric's additive description. Do not let rubric metadata that references specific continuation validation outcomes override patch-structure alignment with the rubric's implementation description.

Close-looking exclusions: A comprehensive test that fails with a test infrastructure error (e.g., 'table already exists' OperationalError) is not evidence of a patch defect; it indicates a test script setup issue with persistent tables from previous runs. Do not penalize the continuation's implementation score for test script infrastructure failures. Additionally, a continuation that only runs state_forwards (not database_forwards) and shows table preservation is testing state-level behavior, not the actual database noop fix.

Abstention boundary: When patch content (actual diff) is not visible and only diff_stat is available, a patch with deletions is a risk signal but not conclusive. If both patches have the same structure (both additive or both restructured) and only validation differs, and validation outputs are consistent with correct behavior, abstain from distinguishing based on validation alone.

experiences.title: FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME redirect fix must not break URL resolution when path is dual-use
experiences.description: Use when a Django admin catch_all_view or similar redirect bug involves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME and the visible code shows the path variable used for both resolve() and redirect construction. The naive path_info→path replacement breaks URL resolution and must not be rewarded as the correct fix.
experiences.context: Applies in Django codebases when the task involves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME not being preserved in admin redirects, specifically in catch_all_view or analogous functions that both resolve URLs and construct redirects. The key visible signal is that the same path variable feeds both resolve() (which expects path_info without SCRIPT_NAME) and HttpResponsePermanentRedirect (which needs path with SCRIPT_NAME). Activate when the visible code shows resolve() usage in the same function as the redirect construction. Do not apply when the function only constructs a redirect without URL resolution, or when the visible prefix does not show resolve() usage.
experiences.experience: The discriminative insight is that catch_all_view uses the path variable for two purposes: (1) resolve() to check if the URL matches a pattern, which requires path_info (without SCRIPT_NAME prefix), and (2) HttpResponsePermanentRedirect to construct the redirect URL, which requires path (with SCRIPT_NAME prefix). A rubric that rewards the naive path_info→path change as the correct fix is semantically misaligned because it breaks URL resolution—resolve() would receive a path with the SCRIPT_NAME prefix and fail to match URL patterns. The rubric should require evidence that the fix separates these uses: retaining path_info for resolve() while using path for the redirect. If the visible prefix shows resolve() usage in the same function, the rubric must penalize the naive fix. If the visible prefix does not show resolve() usage, preserve uncertainty about whether the naive fix breaks URL resolution. Do not prescribe a specific implementation—any visible separation of the two uses is valid. Do not add unrelated query-string or deployment-prefix requirements unless the task or trajectory specifically investigates them.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Separates path variable uses for URL resolution and redirect construction under FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME
reference_golden_rubrics.description: The trajectory should show evidence of distinguishing the path variable used for resolve() (URL resolution, requires path_info without SCRIPT_NAME) from the path variable used for redirect construction (requires path with SCRIPT_NAME). A naive change of path_info→path that applies to both uses breaks URL resolution. Strong evidence includes a diff or edit that retains path_info for resolve() while using path for the redirect URL, or verification that the redirect preserves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME while URL resolution still works. The rubric must not reward the naive one-line path_info→path change as the correct fix when resolve() usage is visible in the same function.

observable_evidence: The catch_all_view function visible in the trajectory uses resolve() with the path variable for URL resolution
The same path variable feeds HttpResponsePermanentRedirect construction
The fix retains path_info for resolve() while using path for redirect construction, rather than naively replacing all path_info with path
avoid_overfitting_to: Rewarding the naive path_info→path change as correct when resolve() usage is visible in the same function
Requiring a specific implementation pattern when equivalent separation of uses is visible
Adding unrelated query string or deployment-prefix requirements not raised by the task
close_exclusions: If the function only constructs a redirect without resolve() usage, the naive path_info→path change may be correct and this rubric should not penalize it
If the visible prefix does not show resolve() usage, preserve uncertainty about whether the naive fix breaks URL resolution

scale.1: No fix attempted; trajectory ends at exploration or bug identification only.
scale.2: The naive path_info→path change is applied to all uses without separating them, breaking URL resolution when resolve() is visible in the same function.
scale.3: The fix partially separates uses or the separation is ambiguous; URL resolution impact is unclear from visible evidence.
scale.4: The fix clearly retains path_info for resolve() and uses path for redirect construction, with some verification that the redirect preserves FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME.
scale.5: The fix correctly separates uses and includes targeted verification that both URL resolution and redirect construction work under FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Naive path_info→path change that breaks URL resolution in dual-use context
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Penalize trajectories that apply the naive path_info→path change to all uses in catch_all_view when the function visibly uses resolve() for URL resolution. This breaks URL resolution because resolve() expects path_info (without SCRIPT_NAME), not path (with SCRIPT_NAME). The rubric should not reward this as the correct fix.

visible_evidence_to_check: The catch_all_view function uses resolve() with the path variable
The same path variable feeds HttpResponsePermanentRedirect
The edit changes all path_info references to path without separating uses
replacement_focus: Evidence that path_info is retained for resolve() while path is used for redirect construction
Verification that URL resolution still works under FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME
boundaries: Do not apply if the function does not use resolve() or if the visible prefix does not show resolve() usage
Do not penalize if the trajectory correctly separates the uses even if the implementation differs from a specific pattern

scale.1: No evidence of the flaw: the trajectory correctly separates uses or the function does not use resolve().
scale.2: Minor evidence: the trajectory mentions the dual-use concern but still applies the naive fix.
scale.3: Moderate evidence: the trajectory applies the naive fix without addressing the dual-use, but the impact on URL resolution is unclear.
scale.4: Clear evidence: the trajectory applies the naive path_info→path change to all uses when resolve() is visible, breaking URL resolution.
scale.5: Most severe evidence: the trajectory applies the naive fix, verifies it, and presents it as correct despite visible resolve() usage that it breaks.

experiences.title: Distinguish Fix Completeness via Diff Stats and Validation Coverage via Executed Test Output for ForeignKey.validate() Manager Changes
experiences.description: When evaluating ForeignKey.validate() _default_manager to _base_manager fixes, the diff_stat directly reveals whether all 3 occurrences were changed (6 +++---) or only 1 (2 +-). Validation evidence requires actual test execution with pass/fail output, not code browsing, grep, file finding, or package installation. Comprehensive validation covers all four contract branches: archived articles validate, non-archived articles validate, non-existent articles fail, and ModelForm validation works.
experiences.context: The issue requires changing ForeignKey.validate() in django/db/models/fields/related.py to use _base_manager instead of _default_manager. The validate method has 3 occurrences of _default_manager that all need updating. A complete fix shows 3 insertions and 3 deletions (6 +++---), a partial fix shows 1 insertion and 1 deletion (2 +-), and no fix shows empty changed_files. Validation must cover: (1) archived articles validate, (2) non-archived articles validate, (3) non-existent articles fail, (4) ModelForm validation works.
experiences.experience:
Activation: When evaluating continuations that modify django/db/models/fields/related.py for ForeignKey.validate() manager references, use diff_stat to assess fix completeness and executed test output to assess validation coverage.

Positive evidence: A diff_stat of '6 +++---, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)' indicates all 3 occurrences of _default_manager were changed to _base_manager — a complete fix. Continuations with this diff_stat have equivalent implementations and should be distinguished by validation coverage, not fix quality. Test output showing all four contract branches with explicit pass/fail assertions (e.g., 'Test 1 passed: Non-archived article valid', 'Test 6 passed: Form validation failed for non-existent article as expected') provides comprehensive validation. Continuations that both reproduce the bug (Form is valid: False before fix) and confirm the fix (Form is valid: True after fix) demonstrate correct validation workflow and should score higher than those that only browse code.

Contradictory evidence: A diff_stat of '2 +-, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)' indicates only 1 of 3 occurrences was changed — an incomplete fix that leaves validation branches still using _default_manager. Test output annotated 'PASSED (unexpected)' is a red flag: the agent itself notes the result is surprising, which often indicates a buggy test rather than a working fix. An empty diff_stat with no changed_files means no fix was applied, regardless of any test activity. A partial fix cannot be confirmed as sufficient even if test output appears to pass, because the test may not exercise the unchanged validation branches.

Close-looking exclusions: grep commands that confirm no _default_manager remains in related.py are code inspection, not behavioral validation — they do not prove the fix works at runtime and must not be credited as test evidence. find commands that locate test files are file browsing, not test execution. Installing pytest but never successfully running tests is environment setup, not validation. When test file paths are wrong (ERROR: file or directory not found, collected 0 items), no validation occurred even if the fix itself is complete. These activities must not be treated as equivalent to running a reproduction script that shows Form is valid: True after the fix. A continuation that reproduces the bug and applies the fix but does not re-run the test to confirm has more evidence than one that only greps or finds files, but less than one that shows the test passing.

Abstention boundary: If a continuation applies a complete fix (6 +++---) but the trajectory is truncated before showing any test re-run after the fix, the fix cannot be confirmed as working — only the diff_stat confirms the code change, not its behavioral effect. If test execution fails due to import errors or missing modules before any test logic runs, no validation evidence is available regardless of fix completeness. Do not infer validation success from code browsing alone; require visible test execution output with returncode and assertions.

reference_golden_rubrics.title: ForeignKey Validation Contract Coverage
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the continuation validates the ForeignKey.validate fix against the full behavioral contract: the reported scenario (archived articles accessible via base manager but not default manager) AND critical edge cases including non-archived articles still validating, non-existent articles still failing validation, and ModelForm validation working correctly. Strong evidence requires executing tests that would fail on the original bug and pass with the fix, covering all these branches. Weak evidence is only running the basic reproduction case or no validation at all.

metadata.oracle_test: The fix changes validation to use _base_manager. Contract requires: (1) archived articles (filtered by default manager) now validate, (2) non-archived articles still validate, (3) non-existent articles still fail validation, (4) ModelForm with base manager queryset validates. A continuation that only tests (1) has incomplete contract coverage.
metadata.judge_focus: Look for executed test commands and their outputs covering all four contract branches. Prioritize continuations that ran comprehensive test scripts showing all cases pass. Deprioritize continuations that only ran basic reproduction, failed to run tests, or only checked the happy path.
metadata.failure_mode: Superficial validation that misses edge cases like non-existent object handling or form integration

scale.1: No validation executed, or only environment setup/dependency installation without any test of the fix
scale.2: Only basic reproduction case tested (archived article validates) - missing non-archived, non-existent, and form validation branches
scale.3: Basic reproduction plus one edge case tested (e.g., non-archived or non-existent), but not all contract branches
scale.4: Comprehensive validation covering archived articles, non-archived articles, non-existent articles, and form validation - all passing with visible test output
scale.5: Excellent contract validation: all four branches tested with clear assertions, plus evidence of running relevant Django test suite or regression tests that would catch regressions

reference_golden_rubrics.title: Fix Completeness - All Manager References Updated
reference_golden_rubrics.description: Evaluate whether the fix changes ALL occurrences of `_default_manager` to `_base_manager` in the ForeignKey.validate method. The validate method contains multiple validation checks (lines ~917-919 and potentially others) that all must use the base manager. A complete fix shows 3 lines changed (6 +++--- in diffstat), while an incomplete fix shows only 1 line changed (2 +-). Continuation 8 has no fix at all.
